records.title: Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938, OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later and Oracle Java SE on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI: a heap overflow in the Base64 decoder that its discoverer chains into pre-authentication code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; fixed in 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts, none confirmed successful against its sensors (CVSS 3.1 8.1)
records.headline: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
records.summary: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-11-17 fix CVE-2026-114938, an out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder that Calif, its discoverer, scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and says it turned into pre-authentication code execution in the default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; Oracle scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity. Only x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI are affected, a trigger proof of concept is public, Calif withholds its product chains, a second researcher claims a working exploit with no release stated, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts without a confirmed success against its sensors, and VulnCheck says a working exploit is available to its customers. NCSC.ch and BACS warn operators to update internet-reachable Java applications and identity services first, and Cisco's advisory, at version 1.3, lists Catalyst Center, IOS XE and ISE as not affected while Siemens lists Siveillance Control, Siveillance Control Pro and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual with no fix yet.
actions: On every x86-64 host with an AVX-512 VBMI processor that runs Java 17, 21, 25 or 27, update the JDK to 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 or 27.0.1.1 (Oracle builds; Ubuntu and Debian packages carry the same fixes under their own build numbers, other distributions use theirs) or 8u513-perf, then restart the Java processes and rebuild containers, internet-reachable applications and the identity, build and artifact servers Calif names (Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, PingFederate) first; where that waits, start the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics, or with -XX:UseAVX=2 on x86-64 hosts only.

records.title: CVE-2026-133968, MONAI Label through 0.8.5: an unauthenticated path traversal in the datastore upload endpoints gives arbitrary file write and code execution, exploited since September 2026 (Amazon says Cairn AI agents found it as a zero-day against East Asian university servers); fixed in 0.8.6, authentication is off by default (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: MONAI Label CVE-2026-133968 exploited since September: upgrade to 0.8.6; authentication is off by default
records.summary: The MONAI Label 0.8.6 security release of 2026-11-22 fixes CVE-2026-133968, a path traversal in the PUT /datastore/image and PUT /datastore/label endpoints of the medical-imaging annotation server that writes files anywhere the server process can write, reachable without credentials in the default configuration; the CVE record says it was exploited from September 2026. Amazon Threat Intelligence reports that a Chinese-nexus operator's Cairn AI agents found it as a zero-day, went from API mapping to arbitrary file write in about 11 minutes and later to a root shell on a university server.
actions: Upgrade every MONAI Label server to 0.8.6 (pip install -U monailabel==0.8.6, or the projectmonai/monailabel:0.8.6 image), because CVE-2026-133968 is exploited and every version through 0.8.5 is affected.

On every MONAI Label 0.8.5 or older server that was reachable from an untrusted network, review it for unexpected file changes before it returns to service, starting with sitecustomize.py, authorized_keys and cron entries that the service account wrote and nobody deployed, because the upgrade does not evict an attacker who is already in.

records.headline: NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update 1.31.9, 1.30.7 or Plus 37.3.0.1
records.summary: F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, while NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Cisco, Siemens and Synology list products with fixes pending or none, Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy and FortiMail not impacted and is still investigating FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and dozens of other products.
actions: On every PAN-OS firewall and Panorama with the HTTP/2 option enabled, upgrade to 12.2.4-h3, 12.1.10-h6 or 11.2.16-h3 or later (12.1.7-h15, 11.2.10-h19 and 11.2.13-h6 are listed with a 2026-11-23 ETA) or disable HTTP/2, because Palo Alto Networks lists CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 as affecting them with that option on.

Update every internet-facing nginx to 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 (NGINX Plus to 37.3.0.1 or 37.0.8.1) and restart the process, because a reload does not replace the running executable; Ubuntu lists the fixes in USN-9159-1 for 16.04 LTS to 26.10, those for 16.04, 18.04 and 20.04 being available with Ubuntu Pro; where the update waits, disable HTTP/2 on exposed listeners, which blocks only CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, since five unauthenticated flaws reach code execution as the worker and Rapid7's proof of concept for one of them is public.

Update every Synology DSM 7.4 to 7.4.1-90080-2 and every DSM 7.3 to 7.3.2-86009-6 (Synology recommends 7.3.2-86009-6 or above for DSM 7.2.x), and on DSM 7.2.x, 7.1 and BeeStation OS, where the fix is listed as ongoing, turn HTTP/2 off under Control Panel, Network, Connectivity, because CVE-2026-123007 affects DSM with HTTP/2 enabled.

records.headline: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, 3.3.14 fix seven memory flaws; a Rails exploit is announced for 25 November: update the interpreter
records.summary: The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 for seven memory-corruption flaws in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, three rated Critical, and says it knows of proofs of concept that reach remote code execution. Veria Labs, which found the case-conversion flaw independently (CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte heap overflow), says Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed without authentication in their default configuration and plans to publish a code-execution proof of concept on stock Rails on 25 November 2026; no exploitation is reported. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life, and the interpreter itself, not a gem, must be updated.
actions: Update the Ruby interpreter to 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14 on every application host, worker, CI runner and container image that runs Rails, Sinatra or other Ruby code that handles untrusted text, rebuild the images and restart the workers before Veria Labs' announced exploit of 25 November 2026, because updating a gem does not fix the interpreter and Rails is exposed in its default configuration.

Upgrade every self-managed GitLab to 19.6.1, 19.5.8 or 19.4.10 (a self-compiled installation rebuilds Ruby 3.3.14 or 3.4.13 instead), because GitLab ships the Ruby fix as an ad-hoc critical patch release and Veria Labs' Rails exploit is announced for 25 November 2026.

records.title: Cleared Windows event logs are not empty: Arctic Wolf shows that clearing an EVTX log truncates it after the first 64 KB cluster and leaves the earlier records in that chunk's free space, where standard forensic tools do not parse or flag them, and recovered a ransomware encryptor's command line this way
records.headline: Arctic Wolf: a cleared Windows event log keeps earlier records in its first EVTX chunk; carve it
records.summary: Arctic Wolf incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log truncates the EVTX file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the record numbers, but the first chunk keeps its earlier records in its free space. On a domain controller the System log held 104 allocated events after the final clear, yet the encryptor's full command line, stamped about three hours before the clear, sat inside the allocated file, and Event Viewer, EvtxECmd and Magnet AXIOM showed none of it; a PowerShell log in a second case held 44 records of which one was allocated.

records.title: Webworm's NtMonitor: Rapid7 finds a custom rebuild of the SoftEther VPN Bridge that removes the open-source tool's detection fingerprints (rebranded metadata, renamed handshake endpoints, a custom handshake watermark, an embedded resource archive and an encrypted configuration), attributed with moderate confidence to the China-aligned actor that targets European governments
records.headline: Rapid7: Webworm hides SoftEther VPN Bridge behind NtMonitor branding, new endpoints and an encrypted config
records.summary: Rapid7 describes NtMonitor, a Windows build of SoftEther VPN Bridge 4.44 that it attributes with moderate confidence to Webworm, the China-aligned actor that ESET documented moving to European government targets in May 2026. The rebuild keeps SoftEther's function of bridging a remote network into the victim's LAN and strips its fingerprints: branding, handshake paths, the handshake watermark, the separate resource archive and the plain-text configuration are all changed, and Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability. Only one antivirus vendor detected the sample on VirusTotal although it has been public since January.

records.title: Hokkaido: resident-register, support-needed and tax data of the cities of Rumoi and Iwamizawa and the town of Shintoku sat on a subcontractor's development PC infected with the K2F information stealer, which GIS Hokkaido links to the NIKKE game launcher; Rumoi's data was still there after its contract ended
records.headline: Hokkaido: municipal data on a subcontractor's PC hit by K2F stealer via a game launcher; Rumoi's contract had ended
records.summary: On 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-19 the Hokkaido municipalities Iwamizawa, Rumoi and Shintoku disclosed that data they gave their contractor GIS Hokkaido was stored on a development terminal of its subcontractor Rimgate that the K2F information stealer infected overnight on 2 to 3 November: up to 71,002 resident-register and 4,503 support-needed records for Rumoi, whose personal data was still on the terminal after its contract ended, 6,001 resident-register and 986 evacuation-support records for Shintoku, and fixed-asset-tax land and building data for Iwamizawa. GIS Hokkaido told ITmedia that the PC launcher of the game NIKKE is involved and would not say whether Rimgate staff ran the game on the work PC; no leak or misuse is confirmed, and none of the data contains the national My Number.

records.title: CVE-2025-42884, SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50: a JNDI injection that an unauthenticated attacker can use to read or change server information, fixed by SAP Security Note 3660969 in November 2025 and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-11-20 (CVSS 3.1 6.5)
records.headline: SAP Enterprise Portal JNDI injection from November 2025 is now on CISA KEV; confirm Security Note 3660969 is applied
records.summary: CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. The flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI environment properties or a URL used in a JNDI lookup in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal (EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50) and read or modify server information; SAP rated it Medium, CVSS 3.1 6.5, and fixed it with Security Note 3660969 on its November 2025 Patch Day. No source names an actor, a victim or how it is chained.
actions: On every SAP NetWeaver AS Java with Enterprise Portal (EP-BASIS or EP-RUNTIME 7.50), confirm that SAP Security Note 3660969 is implemented and apply it where it is not, internet-reachable portals first, because CISA lists CVE-2025-42884 as exploited a year after the fix.

records.title: CVE-2026-129448, Apache Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5: an unauthenticated request to the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes attacker-controlled objects before authentication and runs code on the server; Apache says it is being exploited, CISA lists it, fixed in 6.1.6 (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 6.1.6 or later
records.summary: Apache's announcement of 2026-11-17 assigns CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) to Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, the same flaw it disclosed as CVE-2026-82384 for 6.1.5 in September: the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes vendor extension types before authenticating the requester, which gives an unauthenticated attacker code execution. Apache states the flaw is being actively exploited and CISA listed it on 2026-11-20, while neither describes the attacks; Roller 6.1.6 or later fixes it, and switching XML-RPC off in the administration interface does not help on older releases.
actions: Upgrade every Apache Roller to 6.1.6 or later (6.1.7 is the project's best available release) and, where that waits, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart; treat any internet-reachable instance on an older release as possibly compromised, because Apache and CISA report exploitation and the request is deserialized before authentication.

records.title: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised in France, six more European countries and Switzerland, with France blaming the IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh for the October campaign; Midnight Blue reports six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2
records.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE flaws, Strict mode does not remove them; France blames IRGC
records.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores, and on 2026-11-09 France's foreign ministry attributed that campaign, and only that campaign, to the Iranian unit Shahid Kaveh. More followed: more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops on 2026-11-02, altered cold-room settings at three sites of the French blood service through a supplier, and, per SRF on 2026-11-05, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores in Switzerland. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. On 2026-11-11 Midnight Blue reported six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, and on 2026-11-20 Danfoss published CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in an announced 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient, so removing internet exposure comes first, and BACS's statement of 2026-11-10 that updates fix the known flaws predates the report and does not cover the six.
actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, which do not close the six unpatched AK-SM 800A flaws that Midnight Blue and CCB report, so the interface stays off the internet; change all credentials where compromise is suspected and check the devices attached to the controllers, as BSI advises; and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.

records.title: CVE-2026-76466, Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E: unauthenticated root command execution on clustered devices, listed as exploited by CISA and used in an intrusion F6 investigated, fixed in X15.5.20 with no workaround (CVSS 9.8), alongside same-day hardening releases for Unified CM, Unity Connection and Snort 3
records.headline: Cisco Expressway root RCE is exploited (CISA KEV, F6 incident): upgrade clustered units to X15.5.20 and check them
records.summary: Cisco's disclosure of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 3.1 9.8), which lets an unauthenticated attacker who holds persistent cookies run operating-system commands as root on Expressway-C and Expressway-E configured in a cluster; X15.5.3 and earlier get X15.5.20, X14 and earlier must migrate, and there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that, soon after a public proof of concept appeared, attackers compromised two internet-reachable X15.5.3 devices, reached two internal cluster nodes through one and ran Python scripts for scanning and credential theft, while Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. The same-day hardening releases for the Unified CM family and Unity Connection (up to 9.8, fixed in 15SU5) and for Snort 3 (9.0) are not known to be exploited.
actions: Upgrade every clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier has no fix and must migrate) and, until it is in, limit TCP 4371 to 4372 to the cluster peers' addresses as F6 advises, because CISA lists CVE-2026-76466 as exploited and F6 saw two internet-reachable nodes compromised soon after a public proof of concept appeared.

On every clustered Expressway that was reachable before the upgrade, search erlang.log for a nodeup record naming wombat@127.0.0.1 and check for scanning, SMB, SQL Server and WinRM traffic that starts on the Expressway or its cluster peers, treating a hit as a root compromise, because an upgrade does not evict an attacker who already holds root.

records.title: CVE-2026-102489 / CVE-2026-102490, Zammad helpdesk: a session-hijack remote code execution and a zammad-to-root escalation, both reported exploited since 21 September; 7.2.2 fixes the root flaw on DEB and RPM installs
records.headline: Zammad 6.5.5 emergency-fixes the exploited session-leak RCE on 6.5; 7.2.3 now supersedes 7.2.2 (root escalation)
records.summary: DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. NCSC-NL states both have been exploited since 21 September and CISA listed both in KEV on 2026-10-02; Zammad says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older, and Horizon3 published the root cause and a working exploit for it on 2026-10-07. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, Zammad 7.2.3 of 2026-11-11, a critical security update, supersedes it, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited.
actions: Copy the application and network logs of every self-hosted Zammad instance, then upgrade it to Zammad 7.2.3, the critical security update of 2026-11-11 that supersedes 7.2.2, and add the Remote-User header-clearing line next to X-Forwarded-User in its nginx or Apache2 configuration (the Docker images apply it automatically); 7.2.0 is affected by the 27 advisories Zammad published on 2026-10-06; a 6.5 instance that cannot be upgraded yet gets the 6.5.5 emergency fix from Zammad's new 6.5 package repository, and an older instance that cannot be upgraded goes offline.

On every instance that was internet-reachable on 6.3.0 to 6.5.4 since 2026-09-21, run DIVD's log-check script, and treat a hit, or any DEB or RPM host where code ran as the zammad account, as compromised.

records.title: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration
records.headline: FBI: various actors run ARTEX against many sectors, government included; Microsoft names Storm-0940 and Storm-3358
records.summary: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases; Expel saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report on 2026-10-31 that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated in incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations, and that the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep it in circulation. CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the framework, and Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. Microsoft adds on 2026-11-06 another cluster, the Cambodia-based, financially motivated Storm-3358 targeting financial organisations, and Check Point reads ten exposed operator consoles that show near-autonomous, opportunistic ARTEX campaigns. CERT-EU says AI-driven activity against the EU institutions it protects highly likely involved ARTEX. The FBI's FLASH of 2026-11-13 says a variety of actors have used ARTEX since at least August against sectors including financial services, government, technology and defense, and lists the observed techniques, among them cloud-trust and vendor-credential pivots, Kudu abuse and Active Directory credential theft.
actions: In every Okta org that allows self-service registration, review the accounts created since 2026-10-13 and every Okta Verify enrollment on them, and remove self-created accounts that nobody provisioned.

records.title: Turla's Cereal toolset turns a compromised on-premises Exchange server into the command channel and mail collector at Kazakh and Romanian government bodies, with no attacker infrastructure and no new transport agent registered (ESET)
records.headline: ESET: Turla's Cereal runs the victim's own Exchange server as C2 and wraps transport agents to collect mail
records.summary: ESET found a previously undocumented .NET toolset, Cereal, on a Kazakh government organisation's Exchange server in November 2025 and on a Romanian government organisation's from December 2025, and attributes it to Turla with high confidence. The compromised Exchange server is the command channel, answering requests on web paths that imitate Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover and ActiveSync, and a module injected into the transport service wraps existing transport agents to collect mail, in Romania configured to select messages to or from NATO and EU addresses; ESET could not determine the initial access method.
actions: On every internet-facing Exchange server, compare ncobjapi.dll and wbemcomn.dll in C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem\\ and the Microsoft.Exchange .ni.dll files in the .NET native image cache with the Microsoft originals and list the non-Microsoft assemblies loaded into EdgeTransport.exe, because ESET places the Cereal loader at those locations and Get-TransportAgent shows nothing new.

records.title: CVE-2026-115731, Puppet Enterprise before 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1: deserialization of a crafted agent report gives code execution as the Puppet service user to any holder of a CA-signed agent certificate, and unauthenticated where the CA autosigns; CISA lists it as exploited (CVSS 4.0 9.4)
records.headline: Puppet Enterprise report-deserialization RCE is on CISA KEV; upgrade to 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1
records.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-17 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. A client holding any CA-signed agent certificate can run code on a Puppet Enterprise server as its service user by sending a crafted report, and where the CA autosigns requests without strong verification an unauthenticated attacker can first obtain that certificate; a trigger event has been public since 2026-11-03, and Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1 carry the fix. The same advisory fixed CVE-2026-115732, a certificate-name authorization bypass (CVSS 4.0 9.0) that lets a certificate for a name extending a real host name authenticate as that host; CISA lists only CVE-2026-115731.
actions: Upgrade every Puppet Enterprise server to 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1 (Puppet Core to 9.1.3 or 8.22.2, OpenVox Server to 9.2.0 or 8.18.0; open-source Puppet gets no fix) and, until the upgrade is in, stop the CA from autosigning certificate requests without strong verification and audit the certificates it issued for names that collide with an existing node name, because CISA lists the deserialization flaw as exploited, any holder of a CA-signed agent certificate reaches code execution on the server and a colliding name authenticates as another host.

records.headline: Mitel MiCollab: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 command injection in the conferencing component; patch KB000129195
records.summary: Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0012 of 2026-11-16 covers five flaws in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier, led by an unauthenticated blind command injection scored CVSS 3.1 10.0 and an unauthenticated XML injection scored 9.0 that could run commands. The 10.3.0.18 release that Mitel named as the fix for its July advisory is itself in the affected range.
actions: Apply Mitel's patch KB000129195 to every MiCollab on 10.3 (10.3.0.18) or earlier, including systems already moved to 10.3.0.18 for the July advisory, and until it is in, restrict external access to the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing component, because Mitel scores one unauthenticated flaw CVSS 10.0 and says the five flaws together amplify the impact.

records.headline: Mitel OpenScape 4000: two unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 Platform flaws; upgrade to V11 R2.14 or restrict access
records.summary: Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0013 of 2026-11-18 covers three flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager: an unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw and an unauthenticated command injection, both CVSS 3.1 10.0, and a command injection reachable from the adjacent network (9.6). CVE ids have been requested but not assigned; the fix is V11 R2.14, PLT HF5 on V11 R1.26 or a patch for V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22, and enabling Security Mode restricted access is Mitel's workaround. The advisory says nothing about exploitation, and it is the second critical Mitel advisory in a week.
actions: Upgrade every OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager to V11 R2.14, apply PLT HF5 on V11 R1.26 or Mitel's patch on V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22, and until then enable Security Mode restricted access as Mitel's workaround article KB000129263 describes, because two unauthenticated Platform flaws are rated CVSS 10.0.

records.title: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36: CVE-2026-129289 lets an unauthenticated request smuggle a second FastCGI request into PHP-FPM and run PHP code when the front end reuses FastCGI connections; the release also fixes the session flaw left open in October and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36: FPM request smuggling to code execution; the open session flaw is fixed
records.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19 with fixes for up to 18 CVEs per branch. The most direct is CVE-2026-129289: PHP-FPM keeps unread php://input bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection, so an unauthenticated multipart request can plant a second FastCGI request and run PHP code as the worker, but only behind a front end that reuses FastCGI connections, which standard nginx and Apache setups do not. The release also fixes CVE-2026-115560, left open in October, and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix; no source reports exploitation or a public proof of concept.
actions: On every PHP-FPM server behind nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on or HAProxy in FastCGI mode, switch FastCGI backend connection reuse off until the server runs 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13, because CVE-2026-129289 gives an unauthenticated request code execution as the worker wherever a connection is reused and an application path leaves php://input unread.

records.title: CVE-2026-123890, VMware vCenter Server: an unauthenticated authentication bypass in the Directory Service gives an administrator session; GTIG reports the suspected China-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited it from early September, Broadcom lists no workaround; fixed in 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200 (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: vCenter auth bypass exploited since September (GTIG), no workaround: update to 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 or 9.1.1.0200
records.summary: Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0009 of 2026-11-19 fixes CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service of vCenter that needs only network access to vCenter (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with no workaround and, in Broadcom's words, an emergency change. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor, exploited it from early September 2026 to move from a compromised remote-support appliance to vCenter, forge administrator SAML sessions and extract domain-controller data from guest virtual disks on ESXi; Broadcom's advisory does not state exploitation. Fixed builds are 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200, 9.1.1.0200 and VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.5, and vCenter 7.0 has no public fix.
actions: Update every vCenter Server to 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 or 8.0 U3m (VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x to 5.2.5 through KB88287) now as an emergency change, and until it is in, drop inbound TCP 2012 to vCenter from every address that is not an allowlisted management host, as Google's hardening guidance lists, after testing because TCP 2012 is the vCenter SSO control-interface RPC, because GTIG reports exploitation since early September and Broadcom lists no workaround.

On every vCenter that was reachable from an internal host before the update, list the SSO and local administrators on vsphere.local that nobody created, review the SSO signing material and ESXi authorized_keys files, because the actor extracted the SAML signing key and created accounts, which updating does not undo.

records.title: tcherber: Cyderes finds an access broker's Go toolkit with VPN clients for FortiGate and SonicWall that, once a tunnel is up, maps internal routes and sweeps Active Directory over LDAP; a credential file mixes default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords (more than 500 FortiGate entries) and connection logs show root-level tunnels into multiple victims in May and June 2026
records.headline: Cyderes: 'tcherber' VPN toolkit for FortiGate and SonicWall, credential file mixing default and real logins, LDAP sweep
records.summary: Cyderes' Howler Cell recovered a Go toolkit that wraps OpenConnect for FortiGate and NetExtender for SonicWall, a credential file of more than 500 FortiGate entries mixing default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, and VPN connection logs showing sustained root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments in May and June 2026. Once the tunnel is up the orchestrator maps internal routes and enumerates Active Directory over LDAP, while port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation are manual tools. Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking initial access broker and malware-as-a-service seller and names no victim, vulnerability or firmware version.
actions: Audit every FortiGate and SonicWall VPN gateway for local accounts with default or guessed passwords (guest, admin, test) or passwords that appear in credential dumps, reset or remove them, and search VPN logs since May 2026 for logins by such accounts that are followed by a broad LDAP enumeration from the VPN address pool, because Cyderes found a broker's toolkit and logs showing root-level tunnels into multiple victims.

records.title: CyberPower PowerPanel Business as a SYSTEM script channel on a domain controller: Symantec traces ntds.dit extraction with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss and a side-loaded implant to scripts that the UPS-management service ppbed.exe runs as SYSTEM; Symantec does not say how the console was reached and no actor is named
records.headline: Symantec: attacker ran SYSTEM commands on a domain controller through CyberPower PowerPanel Business, then took ntds.dit
records.summary: Symantec analysed an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business, UPS-management software, as an execution channel on a Windows domain controller: scripts placed in the product's extcmd folder run through the ppbed.exe service as SYSTEM, and the operator iterated scripts until ntds.dit was exported with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss, then side-loaded an implant. Symantec does not say how the attacker reached the console (public advisories or stolen administrator credentials could give that access) and names no actor.
actions: On every host that runs CyberPower PowerPanel Business, domain controllers first, compare the extcmd and temp\\profile\\extcmd folders with the product defaults and compare the extcmd folders and the console's event-to-command assignments with what administrators configured and treat unknown scripts as hostile; where the techniques Symantec lists are found (ntdsutil or esentutl on a domain controller, scripts staged under extcmd that no administrator configured, a side-loaded implant), assume Active Directory credentials are exposed and plan a krbtgt reset and wider credential rotation, because Symantec saw this channel used to export ntds.dit from a domain controller.

records.title: CVE-2026-19707, Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 and 8.6.0: attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response overflows a buffer in the Smart Form Protection feature and can cause denial of service or code execution on the gateway; fixed in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.5)
records.headline: Airlock Gateway: Smart Form Protection buffer overflow can crash or take over the gateway; update to 8.5.3 or 8.6.1
records.summary: Airlock (Ergon) published CVE-2026-19707 on 2026-11-18: attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response can overflow a buffer in the Smart Form Protection feature of Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 and 8.6.0, possibly causing denial of service or remote code execution against the gateway, when the feature is enabled on a mapping whose backend returns certain multi-byte HTML character references (CVSS 4.0 9.5, high attack complexity). The fix is in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1, no source reports exploitation, and Airlock says a compromised gateway could also affect the protection of the other backends behind it.
actions: Move every Airlock Gateway running 8.5.0 through 8.5.2 to 8.5.3 and every one running 8.6.0 to 8.6.1, starting with gateways that have Smart Form Protection enabled on a mapping whose backend serves user-supplied HTML, because Airlock says one backend response can crash or take over the gateway that protects every backend behind it.

records.title: CVE-2026-131914, Idunno.AntiCsrf 0.9.1 and earlier, a defunct anti-CSRF module for ASP.NET WebForms: one unauthenticated POST with a crafted CSRF form field is deserialized without validation and runs code in the IIS worker process; Mandiant observed exploitation in the wild and no patch exists, so the module has to be removed (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: Idunno.AntiCsrf (ASP.NET WebForms) unauthenticated deserialization RCE exploited, no patch: remove the module
records.summary: Mandiant published CVE-2026-131914 on 2026-11-18 for Idunno.AntiCsrf, an open-source anti-CSRF HTTP module for ASP.NET WebForms last released in December 2008: any anonymously reachable page that does not opt out passes a crafted CSRF form field to an unvalidated deserializer, so one POST runs code in the IIS worker process (CVSS 4.0 9.3). Mandiant states that exploitation in the wild has been observed, names no actor, and says the project has no active maintainer or official patch, so the fix is to remove the module, and Mandiant adds that environments with evidence of exploitation should rotate the secrets held in the web configuration and inspect the web root.
actions: Search every ASP.NET WebForms application's Web.config and bin directory for Idunno.AntiCsrf by name, not by file hash because recompiled copies keep the flaw, and remove the module and its DLL, replacing it with a supported anti-forgery mechanism; on any server with evidence of exploitation, such as IIS requests to .aspx pages that returned 302 or 500 with unusually large request sizes, rotate the machineKey, encryption keys and database credentials in Web.config and applicationHost.config, because Mandiant observed exploitation and no patch exists.

records.title: CVE-2026-90817, REDCap 13.3.0 up to 16.0.48 LTS, 17.3.9 LTS and 17.4.3 Standard: an unauthenticated chain from a public survey request through the Data Import controller to code execution on the server, exploited as of 2026-10-07 for cryptocurrency mining and listed by CISA; fixed in 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: REDCap unauthenticated survey-to-RCE chain exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 16.0.49, 17.3.10 or 17.4.4
records.summary: Securifera described CVE-2026-90817 on 2026-09-27, a five-step chain in Vanderbilt's REDCap research-data platform that turns a request to a public survey into code execution on the server without authentication, given a valid public survey hash (CVSS 3.1 9.8). Unit 42 reported it exploited on 2026-10-07 to install Monero miners behind a transient web shell, with cron, SSH-key and shell-profile persistence, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18. The fixed builds are 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard.
actions: Upgrade every REDCap server to 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS or 17.4.4 Standard and, on any server that was internet-reachable on an older build, check for transient Blade-template files under the web temp cache, crontabs, the authorized_keys of every account, ~/.profile and Monero miner processes, treating a hit as a server compromise, because Unit 42 saw the chain used for mining with persistence that an upgrade does not remove.

actions: Upgrade every HPE Networking (Aruba) Mobility Conductor, Controller, Gateway and access point on AOS-10 or AOS-8 to the fixed build of its train (10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7, 10.4.1.14, 8.13.3.1 or 8.10.0.24; AP-5xx access points in a FIPS-compliant environment need the AOS-8.13.3.2-FIPS build or later), and until then confine the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN behind firewall policy, as HPE advises.

records.headline: PHP2Shell: Trend Micro Apex, Mobile Security and Analyzer patches out, Analyzer 7.5 gets none; Quest KACE, NetApp fixed
records.summary: Trend Micro posted Critical Patch build 7351 for Apex Central and build 20113 for Apex One Service Pack 1 on 2026-11-11, each upgrading PHP to 8.2.35 (the Apex One readme does not name the flaw), and its advisory, updated 2026-11-18, names both patches and lists critical patches 1020 for Deep Discovery Analyzer 7.7 and 1082 for 7.6 (none for 7.5, upgrade to 7.6) and for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector, while its Download Center carries a Mobile Security for Enterprise 9.8 SP5 patch dated 2026-11-17 that the advisory row has not caught up with; Quest says all KACE SMA and SDA versions are affected, with SMA 15.0 CU5 and 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix out and advice to block ports 80, 443 and 52230 until applied; and NetApp's advisory lists ONTAP 9 as affected only by CVE-2026-109618, with attacker access as the www user restricted to the PHP jail and hotfix builds from 9.12.1P20HF1 to 9.19.1P4. NetApp says it is aware of public discussion of the vulnerability and none of the three vendors reports an exploited case on its page, although CISA lists both flaws as exploited.
actions: Install Trend Micro's Apex Central Critical Patch build 7351 and Apex One Service Pack 1 Critical Patch build 20113 (both released 2026-11-11; the Apex One readme updates PHP to 8.2.35 without naming the flaw) on every server now and keep their consoles on administrator networks until done; install Mobile Security for Enterprise 9.8 SP5 Critical Patch 10 (build 3461) and the Deep Discovery Analyzer critical patch for the installed version (1020 on 7.7, 1082 on 7.6; 7.5 gets none, so upgrade to 7.6 first); install the critical patches the table lists for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector.
Install KACE SMA 15.0 CU5 or 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix 9.3.313 (9.3.312 where already installed), and until then block inbound ports 80, 443 and 52230 to every appliance, as Quest advises.

records.title: OptimJack: poisoned scripts served by Optimizely, Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly route iPhones to exploit-kit stages, the Optimizely files also carry a crypto clipper and card skimmer, and the University of Basel site loaded a poisoned StorifyMe widget on 2026-11-14
records.headline: OptimJack: Optimizely names the exploited signup-flow flaw; Report URI counts 178 organisations, Zscaler 450+ domains
records.summary: Optimizely says an unauthorized party exploited a flaw in its Web Experimentation account signup flow to impersonate users and add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects, fewer than 5% of its customers, and Report URI counts 178 organisations that served the code on 2026-11-16 while Zscaler ThreatLabz counts more than 450 domains; the Optimizely files carry a crypto clipper and card skimmer. Ohey reports that scripts served by Kissmetrics and StorifyMe gained a loader from 2026-11-13 that routes iPhones to the Coruna and DarkSword exploit-kit stages and that minute-ly's loader was replaced outright; Hudson Rock names 21 web properties, among them the University of Basel's StorifyMe widget, and calls the iPhone stages delivery observations, not confirmed compromises. How the Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly files were altered is unknown.
actions: List every page of your organisation's sites, and of the agencies that build them, that has loaded Optimizely project JavaScript since 2026-11-16, or Kissmetrics i.js, a StorifyMe widget or the minute-ly loader since 2026-11-13, capture the bytes the browser receives and compare them with the provider's own project content (a search for the loader's host name misses the variant that hides it in base64), and where a file carries the injected loader remove it, keep the response bytes as evidence and treat the payment, login and form pages that loaded an affected Optimizely file as exposed to card and session theft.

If your organisation or an agency building its sites has an Optimizely Web Experimentation account, audit every Project JavaScript field for code nobody wrote and rotate the API tokens, session tokens and integration keys tied to it, because the attacker impersonated users on targeted accounts to edit that field.

records.title: CVE-2026-119618, Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 to 2.4.70: a race in mod_http2 assign_headers() corrupts heap memory and leads to remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled; fixed in 2.4.71, Red Hat calls it unauthenticated and claims public exploit research, Axis OS version 6.50.5.10 and higher is affected with no fixed release yet, no exploitation reported
records.headline: Apache httpd mod_http2 RCE: update to 2.4.71 or drop h2/h2c; Axis OS affected, no fix; Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat fixed
records.summary: The Apache HTTP Server project released 2.4.71 on 2026-11-11 to fix CVE-2026-119618, a race in mod_http2 that it rates critical and says can lead to remote code execution in versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70; Red Hat adds that it is unauthenticated, affects only servers with HTTP/2 enabled through the Protocols directive, and that public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit, while no source reports exploitation. Red Hat has fixed RHEL 9 and 10, Debian bookworm and trixie, Alpine and SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 ship 2.4.71 packages, Ubuntu has shipped backported fixes, while a researcher's public test reproduces crashes on 2.4.70 and, per Wordfence, does not show code execution. Axis says AXIS OS version 6.50.5.10 and higher is affected, has no fixed release yet and gives a workaround that turns off HTTP/2 on the device.
actions: On every internet-facing Apache HTTP Server that loads mod_http2, update to 2.4.71 or to your distribution's fixed package (Debian bookworm 2.4.71-1~deb12u1, trixie 2.4.71-1~deb13u1 or forky and sid 2.4.71-1, Ubuntu per USN-9090-1, Alpine 2.4.71-r0, RHEL 9 mod_http2 2.0.26-7.el9_9.1, RHEL 10 mod_http2 2.0.29-5.el10_3.1) and restart it; update SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 to apache2 2.4.71-150700.4.30.1; where no fixed package exists yet, as on the SUSE products still in progress, remove h2 and h2c from the Protocols directive until one does, because Red Hat reports an unauthenticated code-execution path and a public exploit, though it rates its RHEL 9 and 10 packages Important rather than Critical for their harder exploitation.

On every Axis network device on AXIS OS version 6.50.5.10 or higher, set System.HTTP2.AllowH2 and System.HTTP2.AllowH2c to no through param.cgi now (Axis Device Manager mass-deploys it) and install the service release when Axis ships it, then revert the settings, because Axis says an unauthenticated attacker could gain administrator access and has released no fixed AXIS OS.

records.title: Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 published on 2026-11-17, carried a credential stealer that a .pth startup hook runs every time Python starts, collecting environment secrets and requesting Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions OIDC tokens; both versions were removed and 1.26.0 is the last clean release
records.headline: Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI carried a Python-startup credential stealer in 1.26.1 and 1.26.2; pin 1.26.0
records.summary: Socket and SafeDep report that versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's official agent-framework metapackage were published to PyPI on 2026-11-17, about 33 minutes apart, with a .pth file that runs a credential stealer whenever Python starts, so a pip install in a CI job is enough. It collects environment secrets and credential files and requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. Both versions were removed from PyPI and 1.26.0 is the last clean release; how the attacker obtained publishing access is not known.
actions: Search lockfiles, requirements files and CI install logs for agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 installed since 2026-11-17 20:35 UTC, and on every host or job that ran Python after installing either, treat the environment variables, local credential files, Azure managed-identity and Azure DevOps tokens and, for 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens as stolen and rotate them, then pin agent-framework to 1.26.0 or earlier.

records.headline: Oracle CSPU: 56 unauthenticated rows at CVSS 9.0+, six at 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic, BI; none exploited
records.summary: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update of 2026-11-17 carries 655 patches, and its risk matrices mark 56 of the 62 rows scoring CVSS 3.1 9.0 or above as remotely exploitable without authentication. Six are CVSS 10.0 with changed scope, in Oracle Access Manager (three rows), WebLogic Server TopLink Integration, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition, and WebLogic Server and E-Business Suite carry further unauthenticated rows at 9.8. No source reports exploitation of any of these rows, and for attacks that need no privileges Oracle's interim measure is blocking the network protocols an attack needs.
actions: Block T3 and IIOP to every WebLogic Server from networks that untrusted hosts can reach and apply the November 2026 CSPU first to internet-reachable Access Manager, WebLogic Server, E-Business Suite and APEX or REST Data Services instances, because Oracle marks 56 rows at CVSS 9.0 or above as exploitable without authentication and names blocking the required network protocols as its interim measure for attacks that need no privileges.

records.headline: TYPO3: backend user to installer to admin and RCE (SA-027 Critical); Form Framework flaw SA-029 exploited; update now
records.summary: TYPO3 published ten core advisories on 2026-11-17 for 10.0.0 to 14.3.11, fixed in 14.3.12 LTS, 13.4.40 LTS, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS. TYPO3 states that SA-029, a Medium information disclosure in the Form Framework that can become cross-site scripting through uploaded HTML, is known to be actively exploited, naming no actor or victim.

records.headline: RIKEN Fugaku: intruder entered via the public status dashboard, took users' SSH keys and tried them elsewhere
records.summary: RIKEN says that between 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-13 an external party used the publicly accessible web page showing Fugaku's operating status to enter its internal operational network, tampered with internal servers (some with malicious programs) and took or may have taken home-directory files, user-authentication data and credentials users had stored for other systems, such as SSH private keys and access keys. Up to 4,222 Fugaku and 375 Rikyu users are affected, RIKEN confirmed that some of the stolen credentials were tried against other systems, and it suspended Fugaku on 2026-11-14. How the dashboard was breached is still under investigation, and RIKEN names no actor.

records.title: Barracuda's own account of a 44-hour intrusion into its cloud: a key given to an AI vendor and never retired, found in that vendor's compromised development environment, led an intruder across about ten cloud accounts to Kubernetes; notified Managed XDR customers must recreate their integration credentials
records.headline: Barracuda: an unretired vendor cloud key led an ARTEX-consistent intruder across ten accounts in 44 hours
records.summary: Barracuda says an attacker used a valid cloud access key that it had issued to an AI-sector vendor for a past project and never retired, between 2026-11-01 04:33 and 2026-11-02 23:31 UTC, reading stored secrets and moving through about ten cloud accounts, a data analytics system, a source-code token and Kubernetes clusters. One system reached stores the credentials Barracuda Managed XDR uses to collect data from customers' connected systems; Barracuda found no direct evidence they were accessed, treated them as exposed and asked the customers it notified to revoke and recreate them. Barracuda says the activity is consistent with ARTEX, an AI-driven penetration-testing framework, and that this shows how the attacker worked, not who it was.
actions: If Barracuda notified you that your Managed XDR Cloud or Monitored Endpoint integration credentials may be affected, revoke and recreate each integration credential and review activity in the connected systems (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, endpoint security platforms and others) since 2026-11-01; Barracuda says an organisation it did not notify needs no action.

records.title: COLD RELIC: Mandiant shows the FSB-linked group reusing data stolen from one US organisation as the impersonation pretext for the next, then holding cloud tenants through MFA push fatigue and enrolled passkeys, backup codes and MFA devices that survive password and session resets
records.headline: Mandiant: COLD RELIC turns one cloud compromise into the pretext for the next; enrolled passkeys outlive password resets
records.summary: Mandiant reports that COLD RELIC, the name Google Threat Intelligence Group now uses for the group formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057 (Star Blizzard), reused the staff directory and identities stolen from one US organisation in late 2025 to impersonate a contact when approaching a second in 2026. In the late-2025 case it took over a Super Admin account through push-notification fatigue, kept access with enrolled passkeys, MFA backup codes and rogue MFA devices that survived password and session resets, and exported the whole tenant; in 2026 it phished Entra ID credentials and registered a new MFA device to download one user's drive. GTIG names government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America as targets and says new phishing operations continued into November 2026.
actions: In every Google Workspace and Entra ID tenant you run, search the administrator and sign-in logs for passkey, backup-code and MFA-device enrolments on privileged accounts and for tenant-wide Customer Takeout exports, because COLD RELIC's enrolled authenticators survived password and session resets.

records.headline: Craft CMS unauthenticated SQL injection gives admin takeover; CCCS reports exploitation; update to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2
records.summary: CVE-2026-123488 is an unauthenticated SQL injection in the front-end search of Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1 on MySQL and MariaDB that gives read and write access to the database, including setting the admin flag or overwriting password hashes. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security says open source reporting indicates exploitation in the wild and VulnCheck lists it in its own KEV database; no first-hand telemetry or CISA listing was found. Craft fixed it in 4.18.9 and 5.11.2 and offers a query-string block as a workaround.
actions: Update every Craft CMS 4 site to 4.18.9 and every Craft CMS 5 site to 5.11.2 now, and where that waits block front-end requests whose query string contains [attribute] or its encoded form %5Battribute%5D; on each MySQL or MariaDB site that was internet-facing on an older build, check the users table for an admin flag or password hash nobody changed and for administrator accounts you did not create, because the flaw writes to the database and updating does not undo it.

records.headline: BundID: mass automated logins lock citizen accounts; BSI confirms; password sign-in cut on 16 November
records.summary: On 2026-11-16 Germany's BSI confirmed automated, mass login attempts against BundID, the federal citizen account for online administrative services: failed attempts locked accounts and triggered password-reset mails, and the federal government switched off username-and-password sign-in while eID and other sign-in means stayed open. records.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant's quarterly AI threat update of 2026-11-16 reports an exposed multi-agent framework, exploit_agent, that compares code before and after patch announcements, drafts exploits and runs them with no human in the loop, the first such full automation GTIG has identified. records.title: TGR-STA-0049: Unit 42 describes the PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT implants, which use HTTP/3 over QUIC for command and control against government networks entered through unpatched Exchange servers, then spread through domain logon scripts and grant FullAccess on every mailbox
records.headline: Unit 42: TGR-STA-0049 uses QUIC C2, logon-script spread and Exchange FullAccess loops against governments
records.summary: Unit 42 reports that TGR-STA-0049 (also tracked as REF7707, Earth Alux and Ink Dragon) has attacked Southeast Asian government entities since at least July 2025, entering through unpatched Exchange and web servers, and says the group's targeting also includes governments in South America and Europe. Its new PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT implants use HTTP/3 over QUIC as the main command channel in most variants, the operators spread KUKURAT through domain logon scripts after taking a domain controller, and on Exchange they grant a compromised account FullAccess on every mailbox.

records.title: Symantec: a September 2026 intrusion at a US retailer shows attackers switching to AI-generated PowerShell and, about ten minutes after first querying SolarWinds Orion, using the RabbitMQ Erlang cookie bundled with it to run a command on a second server
records.headline: Symantec: AI-assisted retailer intrusion pivots through SolarWinds Orion's bundled RabbitMQ Erlang cookie
records.summary: Symantec reports that after hand-typed commands against a US retailer's web server were blocked, the attackers switched overnight to long, error-free PowerShell scripts and, about ten minutes after first querying SolarWinds Orion, read the Erlang cookie of the RabbitMQ broker bundled with it and ran Orion's own erl.exe to execute a command on a second web server. Symantec assesses AI assistance with high confidence and says no technique was new: the AI supplied speed, while the chain ran through SQL Server command execution, web shells, side-loaded security-vendor executables and domain credential theft.

records.summary: CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9) lets file-transfer actions inside an already-active ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote session run without the authorization or Host-confirmation step the product is meant to require. Huntress documented exploitation from 20 August 2026, over two weeks before ConnectWise's 8 September patch (26.6.5), in which a modified ScreenConnect client automatically pushes the same infection chain to every newly connected Host session, giving the bug a worm-like spread across an MSP's or IT department's own remote-support connections.
actions: Update every ScreenConnect technician host client and Access agent to 26.6.5 or later now, not only the server, because the vulnerable code runs on the technician's machine; where that waits, remove the TransferFiles permission from every role and session group (Administration > Security > Roles).

Treat any pre-26.6.5 client that shows a second, unfamiliar RMM tool or an unexplained ScreenConnect connection ID as compromised and reimage it rather than patching in place, because a technician's session can already have propagated the infection to every host that client connected to.

On every ScreenConnect server, read a copy of App_Data\\Session.db for guest-originated RanFiles or SentFiles events that overlap an open host connection, and on any hit isolate the technician's workstation and rotate every credential reachable from it (RMM, PSA, vault, customer admin accounts), because Huntress saw one workstation fully compromised nine seconds after its client ran a guest-pushed file.

records.title: Fortinet coordinated security hardening release: the advisories published on 2026-11-10 carry unauthenticated FortiMail, FortiAnalyzer, FortiManager, FortiOS and FortiAuthenticator flaws rated CVSS up to 9.8; FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0 have no fixed build for the JSON API flaw, FortiOS 7.0 and FortiMail 7.2 are left out of the October fixes
records.headline: Fortinet advisories: FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0 have no fix for a 9.8 JSON API flaw; FortiMail RCE rows too
records.summary: Fortinet's hardening releases of 2026-10-21 (FortiMail, FortiAuthenticator) and 2026-10-22 (FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer) fixed critical and high-severity flaws, and the advisories withheld until Patch Tuesday were published on 2026-11-10 with critical rows in FortiMail (unauthenticated code execution, SQL injection and IBE account takeover, CVSS up to 9.8), FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager (an unauthenticated JSON API flaw at 9.8, oftp port flaws, FGFM code execution), FortiOS, FortiAuthenticator and FortiClient. The October builds fix most rows, but FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.2 have no fixed build for CVE-2026-126170 until the upcoming 8.0.3 (workaround: set rpc-permit none), and FortiOS 7.0, FortiMail 7.2 and FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 7.0 are left to migrate or wait; none of the 2026-11-10 advisories states exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every FortiMail to 8.0.2, 7.6.7 or 7.4.9 (a 7.2 unit moves to a fixed release; 7.2.10 for CVE-2026-126150 is not released), every FortiAuthenticator to 8.0.4 or 6.6.11, every FortiOS to 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 or 7.2.14 (a 7.0 unit migrates), and every FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer on 8.0.0 or 8.0.1, 7.6, 7.4 or 7.2 to 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.12 or 7.2.13 (7.0 migrates), internet-facing units and FortiMail first, because the advisories describe unauthenticated code execution and account takeover and Fortinet warns that patch differences show attackers where the weakness sits; keep the FGFM and oftp ports and every administrative interface off untrusted networks.

On every FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager (Cloud variants included) on 8.0.0 through 8.0.2, set rpc-permit none on every administrator profile that has the JSON API enabled until Fortinet releases 8.0.3, because no 8.0 build fixes the unauthenticated 9.8 flaw CVE-2026-126170 and 8.0.2 is affected.

records.title: ARTEX against AWS: Datadog sees agent sessions open with anonymous S3 reads, search CloudWatch Logs for secrets with stolen long-term IAM keys, and self-register in public Cognito user pools to obtain AWS credentials
records.headline: ARTEX in AWS: CloudWatch log searches for secrets, Cognito self-sign-up for credentials; hunt CloudTrail for both
records.summary: Datadog Security Labs reports that in October 2026 operators of the ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework worked against several AWS environments with a focus on financial data: sessions opened with anonymous S3 reads, a stolen long-term IAM key drove CloudWatch Logs FilterLogEvents searches for company names, passwords and access keys, and where no key was held the agent self-registered in a public Cognito user pool and traded the tokens for AWS credentials. Datadog says the distributions it studied do not appear to carry a cloud playbook of their own, so the steps follow the model behind them.

last_development.summary: Check Point Research confirms exploitation of unpatched Check Point gateways from 2026-10-30 (PHP2Shell, then the root escalation CVE-2026-123039, exploited against a couple of dozen customers, with a persistent backdoor and an ESXi wiper); the Jumbo takes now carry both fixes.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619 and CVE-2026-123039, Check Point Force, Spark and Cloud firewalls: PHP2Shell on the Mobile Access and VPN web interfaces, chained with a local root escalation, is exploited against unpatched gateways (implant, ESXi wiper); the fix is in Jumbo takes R81.20 take 174, R82 take 132, R82.10 take 52 and R82.20 take 14
records.headline: Check Point gateways exploited (PHP2Shell, root escalation): Jumbo R81.20 t174, R82 t132, R82.10 t52, R82.20 t14
records.summary: Check Point Research reports that from 2026-10-30 an attacker exploited unpatched Check Point gateways through the Mobile Access portal with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), escalated to root with CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8, a local flaw in the dynamic_server process that Check Point says was exploited against a couple of dozen customers), installed a persistent backdoor and in the first wave deleted files on a VMware ESXi host. The fix for both is in Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator R81.20 take 174, R82 take 132, R82.10 take 52 and R82.20 take 14 or later, with none listed for R81.10 or R81, and the standalone PHP hotfix is not stated to cover CVE-2026-123039; sk1000302 itself carries no statement on exploitation.
actions: Install a Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator at or above R81.20 take 174, R82 take 132, R82.10 take 52 or R82.20 take 14 on every Check Point gateway, management server, log server, Multi-Domain server and Maestro, because it carries both the PHP2Shell fix and the fix for CVE-2026-123039, and until it is in apply the cp-httpd.conf mitigation and stop the dynamic_server process; replace R81.10 and R81 systems, for which no fix for CVE-2026-123039 is listed.

On every gateway that ran Mobile Access, SSL Network Extender, SAML-realm VPN, the captive portal, UserCheck or Zero Phishing before the hotfix, search /var/log/dynamicCli.log for commands that do not use the legitimate Clish wrapper and the Mobile Access login-template directory for PHP files nobody deployed, and treat a hit as a compromise, because the implant has backup and snapshot persistence and one attacker moved from a gateway to an ESXi host.

last_development.summary: eMudhra's full incident report of 2026-11-10 says eight RSA-4096 issuers (G2B and G2C) were revoked on 2026-11-07 with the reason cessationOfOperation because their keys were handled in the memory of a Python script, so eMudhra cannot show compliance with its policy; it had said on 2026-10-19 that they were not impacted, no source says the keys leaked, and the G2C issuers had issued end-entity certificates.

records.title: eMudhra: the private keys of eight ECDSA intermediate CA certificates were trivially recoverable, so anyone could forge trusted HTTPS certificates, and eight RSA intermediates were revoked on 2026-11-07 for key handling eMudhra cannot show compliant; browsers block the eight ECDSA intermediates, clients with their own trust store or no revocation checking need an update (CVE-2026-111943 in Go)
records.headline: eMudhra: eight ECDSA CA keys guessable, eight RSA CAs revoked; Windows drops the rest 2026-11-16; update clients
records.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were so weak that anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site, and eMudhra's incident report of 2026-11-10 adds eight RSA intermediates revoked on 2026-11-07 because it cannot show their keys were handled as its policy requires. Browsers and the Apple, Microsoft and Google trust stores block the eight ECDSA intermediates, and Microsoft removes the remaining eMudhra roots from Windows, Edge and WebView2 from 2026-11-16. Software with its own trust store or no revocation checking stays exposed until updated (Go, GitLab, Python, Java, macOS command-line tools, SonicWall DPI-SSL, Cisco IOS XE and ISE), and no exploitation is reported.
actions: Update every non-browser TLS client that keeps its own CA bundle or does not check revocation to a fixed version: standalone Java runtimes, including those already updated on 2026-10-21, to the update of Oracle's Security Alert CVE-2026-114820 or OpenJDK (Oracle Database Server, Autonomous Health Framework and OPatch installations too), Python 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 or 3.11.18 together with pip 26.2.2 or later, Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, self-managed GitLab to a fixed patch release together with GitLab Runner 19.5.1, and SonicWall Gen7 firewalls with Client DPI-SSL enabled to SonicOS 7.3.4-7015 or later and Gen8 to 8.2.3-8015 or later; then confirm with curl against the incident tracker's test host that the client rejects the certificate; on managed Macs update to macOS 27.2.1, 26.7.3 or 15.8.3, or where that is not possible remove emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from /etc/ssl/cert.pem as Apple describes (AAA Certificate Services is optional and can stop tools that read only that file from verifying some unaffected sites).

Replace, by hand where the ACME client does not support ACME Renewal Information, every TLS certificate your organisation holds that chains to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 or to another of the seven certificates Microsoft removed from the Windows and Edge trust lists, or that was issued by one of the eight RSA G2B and G2C issuing CAs eMudhra revoked on 2026-11-07, because Chrome's removal of the G3 root was due on 2026-10-27 and the Windows change takes effect when the trust-list update reaches a device; deliver the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and the trust-list changes Microsoft describes, including its out-of-band update of 2026-10-26, to Windows devices that do not receive automatic certificate-trust updates; do not renew or reissue under emSign Root CA - G1 after 2026-11-16, because Chrome 153 and higher will not trust by default a certificate under it whose earliest SCT is later, and Windows, Edge and WebView2 stop trusting the remaining eMudhra roots on 2026-11-16 as Microsoft's update of 2026-11-10 describes.

Apply Cisco's remediation now for the products its eMudhra advisory (version 1.11) lists with a fix or a procedure available: the CA-trust distrust guide for IOS XE and the guidance for Secure Firewall ASA, FTD and FMC, Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager (run the updatenow command where updates are manual), Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0, Duo Network Gateway 3.4.1, Duo Agentic Authorization Connector 1.0.1 and ThousandEyes Enterprise Agent (Application-hosting Agent 5.2.2).

records.title: CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens industrial and software products (Desigo CC, SIMATIC WinCC, Industrial Edge, Teamcenter and Opcenter among them), Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway, RoomOS and Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches (Guest Shell) in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while most Siemens products, the Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending
records.headline: Brotli flaw: Apple fixes iOS, macOS; Siemens WinCC, UMC, Teamcenter, Opcenter mostly unfixed; Mitel, Cisco listed
records.summary: Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-13 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates), Gridscale X DSA V5.3 and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0 (fixed in V5.4 and V36.8.0), Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix, and, in two interim advisories of 2026-11-10, 15 industrial products including SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, the User Management Component and TIA Administrator and 28 software products including Teamcenter and the Opcenter family, nearly all with no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products with updates planned and workaround articles for three; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2), RoomOS and, at version 1.13 of 2026-11-13, Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches running Guest Shell among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited. Apple fixed the flaw on 2026-11-09 in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 and 26.7.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1 and visionOS 27.2.1, and in HomeView Software 27.2 on 2026-11-12 and tvOS 27.2.1 on 2026-11-13.
actions: Install the latest .NET security updates through Windows Update on every Siemens Desigo CC V8 and V9 host, update Siemens Gridscale X DSA V5.3 to V5.4 and Gridscale X PSS®E to V36.8.0, and update WinCC OA V3.20 to V3.20 P17.1 and BRAUMAT and SISTAR to V8.2 Update 5.

On the SSA-242944 products Siemens lists with no fix or no planned fix (SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, WinCC OA V3.21, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC Companion, the Profiling Tool, User Management Component, TIA Administrator, COMOS Walkinside and the Project Server Web Administration Tool), disable Brotli compression and decompression at the application or proxy layer where it is not required and add the IIS request-filtering rule that denies br in the Content-Encoding header on UMC (on TIA Administrator when UMC authentication is enabled), and on every Industrial Edge Management instance running Common Configurator uninstall all Management Applications and put it behind a firewall or WAF.

Apply Mitel's workaround articles KB000129034 (OpenScape SESAP), KB000129100 (OpenScape SBC) and KB000129114 (OpenScape Contact Center) on the OpenScape SESAP, SBC and Contact Center systems in use, because Mitel has released no update for them.

records.headline: GTIG: stolen cloud keys enable Bedrock and Gemini model services, then resell the quota; hunt the control-plane logs
records.summary: GTIG and Mandiant report 2026 incident-response cases in which actors used exposed or stolen cloud identity tokens (IAM credentials, service-account keys, GitHub tokens) for initial access and then enabled managed model services such as Amazon Bedrock and the Gemini API in victim accounts, ran up charges above USD 100,000 in a single day and resold the quota through proxy gateways. Wiz describes a Google Cloud billing-account variant and Datadog the validation of stolen AWS keys for Bedrock; GTIG lists the audit-log events to watch in AWS, Azure and Google Cloud.

records.title: BluePhishing: Proofpoint's proof of concept turns a consent link for a third-party Entra agent blueprint into tenant initial access, with an agent-creation permission that Proofpoint says cannot be revoked
records.headline: BluePhishing: a consented rogue Entra agent blueprint gives tenant access; Entra users get blueprint rights in November
records.summary: Proofpoint describes BluePhishing, a research proof of concept that extends OAuth consent phishing to Microsoft Entra Agent ID: a victim who consents to an attacker's multi-tenant agent blueprint gets a blueprint principal with an agent-creation permission that Proofpoint says cannot be revoked, and the attacker then creates agent identities, up to 250 per blueprint, that inherit the consented permissions, which Microsoft's documentation says neither the Entra portal nor Microsoft Graph shows. Proofpoint has identified no in-the-wild activity, and Microsoft 365 message MC1506733 says default Entra users can create agent blueprints from 2026-11-04, in a rollout due to complete by late November, unless an administrator turns that right off.

last_update.summary: Insikt gives the persisted file as /opt/vmhostd-core and vmhostd as the process name the implant presents, a name close to the genuine vmware-hostd daemon, and hedges its VMkatz reading: an operator may be able to obtain guest credentials without deploying malware inside each VM.

records.title: GhostFrame: Recorded Future's Insikt Group finds an ESXi post-exploitation framework (vmhostd-core implant, VM control panel, VMkatz credential theft) used by TAG-218, whose activity overlaps Settra ransomware and which targeted SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet VPN appliances in the US and Europe
records.headline: Insikt: GhostFrame implant re-disables ESXi execInstalledOnly every five seconds and steals guest credentials
records.summary: Recorded Future's Insikt Group describes GhostFrame, a command-and-control and post-exploitation framework for VMware ESXi hosts that operators must already hold root on: its vmhostd-core implant persists through ESXi boot scripts, disables the ESXi firewall and the execInstalledOnly control about every five seconds, and a web panel controls guest VMs and runs VMkatz against memory snapshots and virtual disks to recover Windows credentials. Insikt links it to TAG-218, whose activity overlaps Settra ransomware and whose servers targeted SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet VPN appliances in the US and Europe from late August to October 2026.
actions: On every ESXi host that sits behind a SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks or Fortinet VPN appliance that was compromised or unpatched since late August, check for an unexpected executable under /opt, a process masquerading as the ESXi host daemon, changes to /etc/rc.local.d/local.sh, and an ESXi firewall or execInstalledOnly setting that switches itself back off, because Insikt reports the implant resets both controls about every five seconds and re-enabling them without removing its persistence is futile.

last_update.summary: Check Point says the operators placed their tools in existing system directories and renamed SoftEther VPN to system-process names such as vmtoolsd.exe and csrss.exe, so the name, not the path, is the discriminator.

records.title: CopperDragon: Check Point ties three China-nexus intrusion sets to one Sparrow-framework supplier, among them SilentDelivery watering holes on government, shipping, IT and research sites that show a fake Chrome certificate warning (Czech Republic, Germany and France in its telemetry)
records.headline: Check Point: a Sparrow-framework supplier fronts government watering holes with a fake Chrome certificate warning
records.summary: Check Point Research groups three China-nexus intrusion sets under a malware-supply entity it calls CopperDragon, a possible supplier to actors that use the cross-platform Sparrow framework; shared tooling, Check Point cautions, does not prove one operator. The nearest to the constituency is SilentDelivery, which injects script into compromised government, shipping, IT and research websites to replace the page with a fake Chrome certificate warning that pushes a "Certificate Fix" installer carrying the SquadC backdoor, with the Czech Republic, Germany and France among the countries in Check Point's telemetry.
