records.title: CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners that CloudLinux could not reproduce; Citrix XenServer, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu's generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 and Sophos have fixes, Ubuntu 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels are in progress and WatchGuard and Fortinet have none for their products (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Linux TCP use-after-free: Sophos hotfix and Ubuntu generic kernels out; WatchGuard, Fortinet have no fixed build
records.summary: The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path that dates to Linux 4.4 and is reached by a SYN packet carrying IP options; the CNA scores it CVSS 9.8. Anthropic reports that Claude wrote an exploit giving a remote, unauthenticated attacker root on servers with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, which CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce; the Go team says the bug is not specific to MPTCP and Akamai that disabling MPTCP does not prevent exploitation, and no source reports attacks. Citrix rates its XenServer 8.4 and 9 bulletin Critical and names fixes for Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager, XCP-ng released a kernel fix, MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 list the CVE, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ and Amazon Linux kernels are fixed, Ubuntu has fixed its generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 while 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels were still in progress on 2026-11-10, and Sophos has shipped a Firewall hotfix and SD-RED firmware, while WatchGuard (Fireware OS, AP, Dimension) and Fortinet list their products as unresolved or under investigation without a fixed build, Fortinet offering an IPS virtual patch.
actions: On every internet-facing Linux server and every XenServer or XCP-ng host with its Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager appliances, install the vendor's fixed kernel or firmware and reboot, then confirm the running version.

On Veeam estates, run Veeam Updater on the appliances, install the private fix for the Linux helper appliances of Windows-based Backup & Replication and of Recovery Orchestrator 13.1, redeploy virtual labs and helper appliances that stay deployed and replace recovery media made before the update.

On hosts that cannot reboot yet, drop IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options ahead of the TCP stack as CIQ, AWS and Vates describe, after testing on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not close the path.

records.title: CVE-2026-105133 / CVE-2026-105134, AhsayCBS backup management console: an unauthenticated authentication-bypass and code-execution chain exploited since 7 October to drop webshells and a cryptominer; Ahsay's earlier patches were incomplete, and its standard releases v9.17.0 and v10.3.6 now list a patchset for both flaws
records.headline: AhsayCBS chain exploited and in CISA KEV: standard releases v9.17.0 and v10.3.6 list a patchset for both flaws
records.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; v9.17.0 of 2026-11-12, a standard release, carries Ahsay's patchset for both CVEs and turns remote API access and the JSP engine off by default, the v10 standard release v10.3.6 of 2026-11-02 lists the same patchset, the latest partner hotfixes v9.15.2.78 and v10.3.4.55 of 2026-10-27 remain an option, and a server that was reachable before the fix needs a compromise check.
actions: Find every AhsayCBS server your organisation or your managed-service suppliers run, including those on v10.3.4.0 or v9.15.2.59, and install v9.17.0 on v9 or v10.3.6 (current build v10.3.6.14) on v10, or the latest partner hotfix (v9.15.2.78 for v7 to v9, v10.3.4.55 for v10) and reboot after it, now; until then keep the management web interface behind a VPN or an allowlist of trusted addresses.

Compromise-check every AhsayCBS server that was internet-reachable since 2026-10-04, re-image any host with a finding from a trusted backup and rotate the credentials stored on or reachable from it, other backup software on the same network included, because the fix does not remove a webshell or persistence that is already there.

records.title: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating
records.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
records.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating and has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira. Tamedia reports that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom, while PK Softech and the federal bodies say no concrete ransom demand reached them; Publica and several other funds say their insured persons' personal data has presumably left. Cantonal police warn that criminals could use leaked personal and financial data for investment-fraud calls.
actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which can neither confirm nor rule out that its insured persons' data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), the Pensionskasse der Stadt Zug (which reports an elevated but unconfirmed risk that its insured persons' data left), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.

records.title: CVE-2026-123158, OpenSSH Portable before 10.6p2 (*sshole): on Linux with musl libc and no PAM, a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to accounts whose password field is *; NCSC Switzerland issued an advisory (CVSS 3.1 8.1)
records.headline: CISA lists the OpenSSH musl password bypass as exploited; update to 10.6p2 or turn passwords off
records.summary: OpenSSH Portable 10.6p2 of 2026-11-05 works around CVE-2026-123158, a password-authentication bypass on Linux systems that use musl libc and run sshd without PAM, Alpine's default OpenSSH server and OpenWrt among them: a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to an account whose password field is *. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory the same day and has rated the flaw actively exploited since 2026-11-10; Alpine shipped fixed packages for every branch back to 3.16. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-09, and GreyNoise records hands-on logins on its gridpoints from 2026-11-07 that ended in a dropped Python implant; SANS ISC's sensors record attempts from 2026-11-05 and Previdian's from 2026-11-06, QNAP says its NAS systems are not affected, and no source reports a compromised production host.
actions: On every musl-based Linux host that runs sshd (Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto), install OpenSSH 10.6p2 or the distribution's fixed openssh package and restart sshd, because updating the package does not replace the running server, and rebuild container and cloud images from a fixed base; until then set PasswordAuthentication no in sshd_config and restart sshd.

On each such host that allowed password logins while reachable, search the sshd log for an accepted password on an account whose password field is *, and check root's and the default alpine user's authorized_keys for keys nobody added and the init scripts for a service nobody installed, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited and GreyNoise saw both persistence steps.

records.headline: XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers: two of 14 flaws exploited, unauthenticated root RCE; password flaws stay unfixed
records.summary: VulnCheck, as CNA, published 14 CVEs on 2026-11-12 for XWEB EVO, the end-of-service Copeland and Dixell web supervisor for refrigeration and cold-chain equipment, seven of them scored CVSS 4.0 9.2 to 9.3: unauthenticated command injection that runs as root, a hard-coded Administrator password, and Administrator and root passwords computed from the device MAC address and date. VulnCheck's sensors recorded exploitation of an unauthenticated configuration write (CVE-2026-124014) from 2026-11-12 and root-command probes against CVE-2026-124010 from 2026-11-13, by opportunistic scanners it does not tie to the October refrigeration attacks. The injection flaws are fixed on the current firmware branch, while the password flaws reach the last firmware, 5.8.8, and stay unfixed because Copeland ended software support on 2026-03-16; Copeland tells operators to remove all XWEB EVO units from the public internet.
actions: Find every Dixell or Copeland XWEB EVO supervisor reachable from the internet and put it behind a VPN now; on each unit that was exposed, review its users, alarm settings and setpoints and read cabinet temperatures directly, because VulnCheck sees two of its unauthenticated flaws exploited and the password flaws will never be fixed.

records.title: CVE-2026-125350, Google Chrome before 157.0.8103.50: a use-after-free in the XML component is exploited in the wild and listed by CISA; Edge 157.0.4341.46 and Edge for Android carry the fix, other Chromium browsers are still to follow
records.headline: Chrome zero-day CVE-2026-125350 exploited: update Chrome to 157.0.8103.50 and Edge to 157.0.4341.46 or later
records.summary: Google's Stable-channel update of 2026-11-09 says an exploit for CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free in Chromium's XML component, exists in the wild; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10 and no source describes the attacks. The fix is in Stable 157.0.8103.50 (Linux) and 157.0.8103.50 or .51 (Windows, macOS) and in Extended Stable 156.0.8078.96, all of 2026-11-09, later Stable and Extended Stable builds of 2026-11-11 include it, and Microsoft's notes list the fix in Edge 157.0.4341.46 of 2026-11-09 and in Edge for Android 157.0.4341.53.
actions: Update Chrome to the current Stable build, 157.0.8103.78 or later (157.0.8103.50 is the first fixed build), and Extended Stable to 156.0.8078.100 or later on every managed endpoint, force the browser relaunch now, update Edge to 157.0.4341.46 or later and Edge for Android to 157.0.4341.53, and install the other Chromium-browser updates as soon as each vendor lists CVE-2026-125350 as fixed.

records.title: The Gentlemen affiliate: an SSL-VPN account without MFA, a Windows Server 2003 host and a dormant local administrator gave Domain Admin in under an hour; the GPO locker most likely lost a replication race, so antivirus was disabled estate-wide but only one host was encrypted (Ransom-ISAC)
records.headline: Ransom-ISAC: Gentlemen affiliate, VPN without MFA to Domain Admin in an hour; GPO locker likely lost a replication race
records.summary: Ransom-ISAC's incident-response report describes an early-August 2026 intrusion by a Gentlemen ransomware affiliate that began with an SSL-VPN account without MFA and reached Domain Admin in under an hour, most likely with credentials taken from an end-of-life Windows Server 2003 host that a dormant local administrator account opened, then used a Rust credential harvester and the EtherRAT implant. The locker's GPO disabled antivirus across the estate but the task that runs it most likely never reached clients because of a replication race, so the locker ran on one host; the report names the telemetry at each step. Single source, no victim named.

records.title: ScreenConnect: Huntress finds 2,223 fake guest sessions named after crypto exchanges on 118 self-hosted servers, enrolled from 2026-11-03 and, in its leading hypothesis, bait for technicians whose clients predate 26.6.5; it saw no malicious use and no overlap with SCKit
records.headline: Huntress: 2,223 crypto-named fake sessions sit on 118 ScreenConnect servers, likely bait for unpatched technicians
records.summary: Huntress counted 2,223 unauthorized guest sessions on 118 self-hosted ScreenConnect servers at 109 MSP and organisation accounts, enrolled between 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-13 and named after crypto exchanges; on the 29 servers with complete history an operator revisited every 151 seconds to keep them online. Huntress's leading hypothesis, which it has not observed, is that they are bait for a technician with a client older than 26.6.5 to connect, so that CVE-2026-84869 runs a file on the technician's workstation; it saw no malicious activity from the sessions and found no overlap with the SCKit indicators.
actions: On every self-hosted ScreenConnect server your organisation or its IT providers run, list guest sessions with an exchange-and-role name or empty company or site fields, copy App_Data\\Session.db and its WAL file before deleting any, and where a technician connected to one from a client older than 26.6.5, inspect that workstation's ScreenConnect Temp and Startup folders and process history and treat text sent through the session as exposed credentials, because Huntress suspects the sessions are bait for the file-transfer flaw CVE-2026-84869.

records.title: PolinRider: a North Korea-linked loader reaches developers through force-pushed forged commits in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories, hijacked npm releases and a fake employer's take-home test, and reads its server address from an Ethereum wallet
records.headline: PolinRider: forged backdated commits, npm hijacks and a fake recruiter run a loader at build or folder open
records.summary: Apiiro found the PolinRider loader in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories owned by 2,330 accounts, where stolen GitHub access force-pushes a copy of the owner's own commit, with the same author, message and date, plus a loader hidden after hundreds of spaces in a build configuration file. Sonatype found the same loader in 12 hijacked npm releases and JFrog in a fake employer's take-home test and scripted camera check; none relies on an npm install script, the server address is read from an Ethereum wallet, and removing the code does not revoke the access that pushed it.
actions: Search every branch of your organisation's and suppliers' GitHub repositories for a semicolon followed by 200 or more spaces in JavaScript, TypeScript and build configuration files, and for .vscode/tasks.json tasks that run node when a folder opens; on any hit, rotate every GitHub and npm token reachable from the developer machines and CI runners that built the repository and review force-pushes, deploy keys, Actions secrets and releases since the infection, because deleting the loader does not revoke the access that pushed it.

last_update.summary: The sentence on when the injected loader runs now cites Microsoft Threat Intelligence, which states it, and a neighbouring clause is shortened to keep the analysis within its length.

last_development.summary: Cursor's own report of 2026-11-13 gives the origin the entry lacked: an access key Cursor issued to its vendor Fireworks AI was exposed, the attacker copied a bucket of coding-agent traces holding some unredacted credentials, and a stolen credential let it write the extension onto the marketplace cache; Open VSX never carried it and the last attacker activity, on 2026-11-01, was blocked.

records.title: Cursor marketplace: a tampered Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) planted an SSH key, a reverse tunnel and persistence for about eleven hours on 2026-10-29; uninstalling it does not remove the persistence
records.headline: Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor
records.summary: Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension; coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor says the attacker could not log in there. Cursor's report of 2026-11-13 says the chain began with an access key it had issued to its vendor Fireworks AI, exposed by Fireworks, which gave the attacker a storage bucket of coding-agent traces holding some unredacted credentials, and that a stolen credential from the exposed data let the attacker write the extension straight onto the marketplace cache; Cursor says this was not a vulnerability in Anthropic's product.
actions: On every developer endpoint that runs Cursor, check extension-install telemetry for Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 installed between 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29; where it is found, isolate the host, remove the unauthorized SSH key, the persistence and any running tunnel process, because uninstalling the extension removes none of them, and rotate every credential reachable from the host from a trusted system.

Ask the admin of every Cursor team your organisation uses whether Cursor's email listing exposed keys arrived, and rotate every key it lists, because Cursor says coding-agent traces from sessions outside Privacy Mode held unredacted credentials.

records.title: Kaspersky GERT BlackNevas case: credentials from systems outside the virtualisation layer reach both vCenter appliances, a remote-access agent and a VMware-lookalike tunnel service persist, vCenter Host Profile remediation switches SSH on across the ESXi hosts, backups are destroyed first and a wipe of the datastores detonates over ten days, with no vulnerability exploited
records.headline: Kaspersky: BlackNevas used vCenter Host Profiles to enable SSH on ESXi, destroyed backups first, then wiped datastores
records.summary: Kaspersky GERT describes a ten-day engagement in which an adversary, identified as BlackNevas from its ransom notes, used credentials taken from systems outside the virtualisation layer to reach both vCenter appliances, persisted on one with a remote-access agent and a tunnel installed as a VMware-lookalike systemd service, then used vCenter Host Profile remediation to switch SSH on across four ESXi hosts, destroyed the backup environment first and detonated a wiper-capable locker that took every virtual machine. Kaspersky states no initial access vector, victim sector or country, and no virtualisation-layer vulnerability was exploited.

records.title: CVE-2026-105437, GitLab self-managed 19.5.4, 19.4.6 and 19.3.8 critical patch release: a heap overflow in Git's merge code that a user who can open a merge request can trigger for command execution as the git user on the Gitaly node; Git 2.56.1 also fixes CVE-2026-111760, code execution when a malicious repository is cloned with submodules; no exploitation reported
records.headline: GitLab critical patch: a merge request can reach a Git heap overflow on Gitaly; update to 19.5.4, 19.4.6 or 19.3.8
records.summary: GitLab shipped an ad-hoc critical patch release on 2026-11-10 for CVE-2026-105437, a heap overflow in Git that, per GitLab, any user who can create a project and open a merge request reaches, and that can run commands as the git user with access to every repository on that Gitaly node. Git 2.56.1 and its backports fix the same flaw and five others, among them CVE-2026-111760, code execution when a malicious repository is cloned with --recurse-submodules; no source reports exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab to 19.5.4, 19.4.6 or 19.3.8 now (self-compiled installs rebuild the Git in Gitaly and the Git at git.bin_path, or move the distribution Git to 2.56.1 or later) and, where that waits, limit who can create projects and sign up, because a user who can open a merge request reaches the flaw and code execution gives access to every repository on the Gitaly node.

records.title: CVE-2026-123710 and CVE-2026-110697, Red Hat Quay: an anonymous client can install its own registry signing key and read or overwrite every private image (CVSS 3.1 9.8), and a low-privilege account can steal other tenants' robot tokens (9.9); fixed in Quay 3.9.28 to 3.18.3, no fix for Quay 5 or the mirror registry, no exploitation reported
records.headline: Red Hat Quay: anonymous signing-key takeover and cross-tenant token theft; update to your branch's fixed release
records.summary: Red Hat's CNA records say an unauthenticated client of Red Hat Quay can obtain an anonymous registry token, present it to the service-key rotation endpoint and install its own signing key (CVE-2026-123710, CVSS 3.1 9.8), and that an account that can create a namespace containing an underscore can retrieve other tenants' robot tokens (CVE-2026-110697, 9.9). Red Hat fixed both in Quay 3.9.28, 3.10.28, 3.12.24, 3.14.10, 3.15.9, 3.16.7, 3.17.7 and 3.18.3, lists Quay 5 and the mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift 2 as affected with no fix, and NCSC Switzerland lists exploitation as unknown.
actions: Update every Red Hat Quay registry to its branch's fixed release (3.9.28, 3.10.28, 3.12.24, 3.14.10, 3.15.9, 3.16.7, 3.17.7 or 3.18.3) and, until then, restrict the /keys endpoint at the proxy or load balancer to trusted internal components; on any instance whose /keys endpoint untrusted clients could reach, review audit logs for service_key_rotate and service_key_delete events with a null expiration_date and remove unrecognised approved service keys, because deleting a rogue key is not durable before the fix and resetting passwords or regenerating robot tokens does not revoke it.

records.headline: Ivanti EPM Core: unauthenticated SQLi to RCE, NCSC-NL reports public PoC; no exploitation known; update to 2024 SU8
records.summary: Ivanti's CNA records of 2026-11-10 describe CVE-2026-121653, an SQL injection in the Core of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before 2024 SU8 that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker reach remote code execution (CVSS 3.1 9.8), and CVE-2026-121683, missing authentication in Ivanti Cloud Services Application 5.0.8 that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker add and delete trusted EPM Core certificate entries (9.4). NCSC-NL reported on 2026-11-13 that public proof-of-concept code for the first flaw now exists and says this raises the chance of exploitation in the short term; Ivanti says it has no evidence of exploitation, and CERT-FR lists Cloud Services Application 5.0.8.1 as the fixed build.
actions: Upgrade every Ivanti Endpoint Manager Core server to 2024 SU8 or later now and every Cloud Services Application 5.0.8 to 5.0.8.1, because NCSC-NL reports public proof-of-concept code for an unauthenticated SQL injection that reaches code execution on the server that distributes software to the managed endpoints.

last_development.summary: Microsoft's analysis describes RelayTrap, a rogue client built on the endpoint to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, and browser-cookie routines designed to push tools through the Shared Toolbox; ConnectWise says clients 26.6.5 and later block the transfer, and a second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations, one with a self-hosted RMM+, so every technician client now belongs on the action list.

records.title: ScreenConnect: commands pushed through Run Command to at least 288 managed endpoints at 48 Huntress customers within 90 minutes on 2026-11-11 installed a rogue second client and the SCKit toolkit; Huntress links the activity to the RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key
records.headline: ScreenConnect SCKit: second wave hits on-prem; disable RMM+, update technician clients to 26.6.5+
records.summary: Huntress saw an operator use access to several cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels on 2026-11-11 to run Run Command as SYSTEM on groups of managed endpoints, installing an attacker-controlled second ScreenConnect client and the SCKit toolkit on at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations within 90 minutes; Sophos independently saw the same client deployments. Huntress later said the activity seems related to the third-party RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key; ConnectWise's CNA record CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) says the extension uses a static API secret by default, names no fix and gives disabling as the mitigation, while a Huntress spokesperson says the panel-access vector is still unclear and Blackpoint calls the extensions' role unresolved. A second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations (Huntress) and appears to target on-premises instances with mitigations pending (Blackpoint); Microsoft describes a rogue client built to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, which ConnectWise says ScreenConnect clients 26.6.5 and later block.
actions: On every ScreenConnect instance your organisation or its IT providers run, disable the RMM+ extension immediately, verify it stays disabled and do not re-enable or reinstall it (on-premises instances by hand; ConnectWise removed it from cloud-hosted ones), review Run Command and Toolbox history and the instance audit logs for executions nobody started, including before 2026-11-11, and check managed endpoints for a second ScreenConnect client service; open no interactive session to a suspect host, use EDR live response or WinRM, because a session can trigger the toolkit to spread to the technician's workstation; update every technician host client to ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later, because a cloud-console update does not update them.

records.title: Luna Moth returns to law firms that likely did not pay, with a token handoff: a video-call 'IT support' agent has the employee copy a Microsoft Graph access token out of Microsoft 365 Copilot through browser developer tools, then bulk-downloads files from the attacker's own server (ReliaQuest)
records.headline: ReliaQuest: Luna Moth has staff hand over a Graph token from Copilot on a video call; no sign-in event follows
records.summary: ReliaQuest reports that the data-extortion group Luna Moth (Silent Ransom Group) returned in October and early November to law firms it had extorted in May and August, using a technique it calls almost certainly new for the group: on a video call posing as IT support the attacker has the employee open Microsoft 365 Copilot, copy the Microsoft Graph access token out of the browser's developer tools and paste it to a text-sharing site, then replays it from its own server and downloads thousands of files in about an hour. The token was issued to the victim's compliant device, so no sign-in event is generated for the attacker's address; ReliaQuest is the only source and names no victim or country.

records.title: CyberStrikeAI turned on AWS: Elastic reads one server's 16 days across eight identities in four accounts, 56 user-data reads in 141 milliseconds, and why six detections each rated medium or low and only the source address tied them together
records.headline: Elastic: CyberStrikeAI against AWS, six medium or low alerts joined only by source IP; alert on user-data bursts
records.summary: Elastic Security Labs reports that between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-16 one server running the open-source CyberStrikeAI platform used the credentials of eight AWS identities (five IAM users, three EC2 instance roles) across four accounts, reading secrets and EC2 user data and, in one case, issuing a Systems Manager command. Every step is a call a legitimate role makes daily, so six detection rules each fired at medium or low severity and only the shared source address showed they belonged to one intrusion; Elastic does not know how the credentials were obtained and names no victim.

records.title: Device-code phishing disguised as a Microsoft Teams meeting booking: Huntress traces an October intrusion from a spear-phish through a Microsoft Safe Links-wrapped Google share link to a scheduler page whose 'Booking Reference' is the device code, an in-browser decrypted kit that restarts the flow when MFA is required, and a token replayed through a residential proxy
records.headline: Huntress: device-code phishing posing as a Teams booking skips URL reputation checks; hunt Cmsi:Cmsi sign-ins
records.summary: Huntress describes a mid-October 2026 intrusion in which a spear-phish impersonating a company executive led, through a Safe Links-wrapped Google share link that sidestepped URL reputation checks, to a fake Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler whose 'Booking Reference' is a Microsoft device code, with a phishing kit shipped as AES-256-GCM ciphertext that the browser decrypts and a fallback that restarts the device-code session when MFA is required. The account had no MFA enrolled and the captured session was replayed from a residential proxy, showing as a device-code (Cmsi:Cmsi) sign-in followed by programmatic user agents; Huntress names no victim country and no Swiss link.

records.headline: ANSSI's second REACTIV report: 64 new breaches, reuse of stolen secrets the one technique; SMS 2FA and IDOR cases
records.summary: ANSSI's situation report of 2026-09-30 for its REACTIV operation counts 99 data breaches reported to it by French state services since 2026-08-01, 67 confirmed, and names the recurring causes: mass exploitation of the Metabase SQL injection CVE-2026-72898 (nine ministry instances compromised), infostealer-harvested credentials used on exposed services without a second factor, IDOR flaws, missing or weak MFA, and compromise through a supplier. The figures are provisional. records.title: DarkLunnen: Group-IB's exposed operator directory shows mass exploitation of FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that plants a 'service' super_admin account, a 4,725-target Swiss FortiGate scan list and restic access to an S3 backup repository at a 'Swiss domain'; Group-IB does not confirm any Swiss victim
records.headline: Group-IB: DarkLunnen's FortiOS chain leaves a 'service' super_admin; Swiss FortiGates are scan targets only
records.summary: Group-IB found an open directory on a Latvian server that documents more than 14 months of operations against Europe by an operator it tracks as DarkLunnen and links to no known actor: a modified public exploit for FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that creates an administrator named service with super_admin privileges, among other tools. Group-IB recovered a list of 4,725 Swiss FortiGate scanning targets, which it says does not confirm vulnerability or exploitation, and restic commands that accessed an S3 backup repository at a Swiss domain in May and June 2025, without naming an organisation or confirming success.
actions: On every FortiGate on FortiOS 7.0 below 7.0.17 (and FortiProxy 7.2 below 7.2.13 or 7.0 below 7.0.20) take the HTTP/HTTPS administrative interface off internet-facing interfaces, and on any unit whose interface was ever reachable list the administrators for an account named service or any unexplained super_admin account and review jsconsole logins; where one is found rotate every secret stored in the configuration, because a patch does not remove an account that already exists.

records.title: WFX Phantom: stolen GitHub tokens push a CI secret stealer into repositories from 2026-11-10, steal Actions secrets, runner memory and cloud tokens, plant AWS and Azure persistence designed to outlast rotation and delete the workflow runs; StepSecurity counts more than 63,000 probe pull requests
records.headline: WFX Phantom: stolen GitHub tokens push a CI stealer; cloud persistence meant to survive rotation; check for probe PRs
records.summary: StepSecurity and Aikido report that from 2026-11-10 an attacker uses stolen GitHub tokens, not a GitHub Actions bug, to open probe pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" and then push a stealer script into workflows, CI scripts or npm hooks where the token's permissions allow, taking Actions secrets, runner memory and cloud credentials, planting AWS and Azure persistence and deleting the workflow runs. Counts differ by lab and time (more than 63,000 probes; at least 1,835 repositories where the payload ran); how the tokens were obtained is unknown, and no Swiss victim is named.
actions: In every GitHub organisation you or your suppliers administer, search for pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" and for commits titled "ci: refresh build cache", "ci: restore", "ci: cleanup", "chore: add ci helper" or "chore: add dependency audit workflow"; for each account that pushed one, revoke its tokens, rotate every secret its workflows could read and remove the AWS trust-policy changes, access keys and Azure federated credentials the stealer created, because the persistence is designed to outlast rotation.

records.title: SignDrop: a public Windows local privilege escalation to SYSTEM that turns Microsoft's CLFS authentication mitigation against itself through Defender's signature-update RPC; proof of concept published 2026-11-10, no CVE and no patch, no exploitation reported
records.headline: SignDrop: public Windows LPE to SYSTEM through CLFS and Defender; no CVE or patch; check CLFS authentication Mode
records.summary: Cyderes Howler Cell reproduced SignDrop, a Windows local privilege escalation from a standard user to SYSTEM that was published on GitHub on 2026-11-10, the day of Patch Tuesday, with no coordinated disclosure, no CVE and no patch. It makes Defender's signature-update RPC and symbolic links get clfs.sys to write a SYSTEM-owned authentication file where the attacker chooses, so it applies where the CLFS authentication Mode is 0 or 1; no exploitation is reported, Microsoft has not commented, and the researcher's claim that about 80% of Windows installations are exposed is unsubstantiated.

records.title: CVE-2026-126325, PTC Windchill and FlexPLM: deserialization of untrusted data lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run code (CVSS 4.0 9.2, high attack complexity); PTC announced a patch on 2026-11-11 and keeps the fixed releases behind its support login, no exploitation is reported, and an earlier Windchill flaw was exploited in June
records.headline: PTC Windchill and FlexPLM: new unauthenticated deserialization RCE patched 11 Nov; fixed releases behind PTC login
records.summary: PTC's CNA record, restated by NCSC Switzerland and BSI, says CVE-2026-126325 lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run code on PTC Windchill and FlexPLM through deserialization of untrusted data (CVSS 4.0 9.2, high attack complexity), in eleven Windchill and ten FlexPLM release lines. PTC announced a patch on 2026-11-11 (its advisory sits behind a customer login, so no fixed release is public) and has already patched PTC-hosted environments; no source reports exploitation of this flaw, although CISA listed an earlier Windchill and FlexPLM RCE as exploited in June.
actions: Apply the patch PTC announced on 2026-11-11 (article CS483249 in PTC's support portal, login required) to every self-hosted Windchill and FlexPLM, internet-reachable servers first, and keep them off networks that untrusted hosts can reach until it is in, because the flaw needs no authentication and PTC names no workaround.

records.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: 28 flaws fixed on 2026-11-12, among them CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) in packet processing on every deployment in default configuration, plus an unauthenticated NetScaler Console authentication bypass (CVE-2026-120869); no exploitation reported
records.headline: NetScaler: 28 flaws fixed, one reaches every default ADC and Gateway; update to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39
records.summary: Cloud Software Group's bulletin CTX697305 of 2026-11-12 fixes 28 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway, 9 of them scored CVSS 4.0 9.0 or above; CVE-2026-120868 (9.3) needs no feature or authentication and affects every deployment in default configuration, and CVE-2026-107412 (9.5) reaches Gateway and AAA virtual servers. The fixed builds are 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS and 13.1-37.293, and bulletin CTX697320 fixes an unauthenticated NetScaler Console authentication bypass in 14.1-74.34; the bulletins describe the impact as unpredictable behaviour or denial of service, offer no workaround and state no exploitation status, while CERT-EU writes that Citrix reports none and no source reports an attack.
actions: Upgrade every customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway to 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39 (14.1-73.58 FIPS; 13.1-37.293 for 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP) and the NetScaler Console to 14.1-74.34, internet-facing Gateway and AAA appliances first, because CVE-2026-120868 affects every unpatched appliance in default configuration and neither bulletin offers a workaround; keep the management address (NSIP) and the Console IP off networks that untrusted hosts can reach.

records.title: CVE-2026-111497 / CVE-2026-70197, Microsoft .NET: an out-of-band release fixes a Brotli decoder flaw and delivers the Windows sockets fix that the 13 October update did not contain, in 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14 (CVSS 3.1 8.1)
records.headline: Microsoft ships out-of-band .NET fixes: hosts updated on 13 October still carry the Windows sockets flaw
records.summary: Microsoft released .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3 out of band on 2026-10-25 to fix the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS 3.1 8.1, publicly disclosed, rated Exploitation More Likely) and to deliver the corrected fixes for CVE-2026-70197 (Windows sockets memory corruption, CVSS 3.1 8.1) and CVE-2026-102870 (Blazor debugger), which the 2026-10-13 release did not fully address. Brotli exposure needs an application that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data, which ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not do by default; CISA lists CVE-2026-111497 as exploited since 2026-10-27, although Microsoft's record still said not exploited on 2026-10-25 and no source reports an attack on .NET. Microsoft's record, revised on 2026-11-12, also lists Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2019 to 2025 as affected, with the November 2026 cumulative updates as the fix.
actions: Install .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (11 Release Candidate 3 for the preview) on every host that runs .NET applications, including Windows hosts already updated on 2026-10-13, which still carry CVE-2026-70197; rebuild and republish self-contained applications and rebuild container images from the updated .NET images, because a runtime update on the host does not change a bundled runtime; install the November 2026 Windows cumulative update of each branch (KB5131096, KB5131085, KB5131090, KB5131080, KB5131087, KB5132061 or KB5132059) on every Windows endpoint and server, because Microsoft's record now lists Windows as affected and CISA lists the flaw as exploited.

last_development.summary: Siemens revised SSA-834709 to V1.2 on 2026-11-10 and added a second affected configuration for each of the four IoT2050 variants, all versions running Example Image versions with Node-RED installed, for which no fix is available; the V4.3.4-1 fix and the interim mitigations apply only as stated for Industrial OS and Node-RED.

records.title: CVE-2026-58115, Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM ship a Node-RED interface with no authentication, so one unauthenticated HTTP request runs code with maximum privileges on an OT edge gateway (CVSS 10.0); VulnCheck's canary caught exploitation
records.headline: Node-RED flaw in Siemens IoT2050 hit a VulnCheck canary; V4.3.4-1 fixes Industrial OS, Example Image has no fix
records.summary: Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709 of 2026-08-11 discloses CVE-2026-58115, rated 10.0 on both CVSS 3.1 and 4.0: SIMATIC IoT2050 devices with Node-RED installed do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, so an unauthenticated attacker with network reach can create a flow and run code with maximum privileges. Siemens' advisory, revised on 2026-11-10, lists the Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants in two configurations: all versions below V4.3.4-1 running Industrial OS, fixed in V4.3.4-1, and all versions running Example Image versions, for which no fix is available; Siemens offers uninstalling or hardening Node-RED as interim mitigations. VulnCheck reports that on 2026-10-30 one of its canaries caught exploitation, a single request that deployed a flow downloading and running a Linux bot, with web-shell flows from the same address since; the target was a canary and the activity looks like opportunistic mass scanning.
actions: Update every SIMATIC IoT2050 running Industrial OS (Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM) to V4.3.4-1 or later now; on units running Example Image versions, for which Siemens has no fix, and wherever the update cannot happen at once, uninstall Node-RED if it is unused or harden it as Siemens' Node-RED User Guide describes and take its HTTP interface off networks that untrusted hosts can reach, since exploitation takes a single unauthenticated request.

On every Node-RED instance that was reachable from an untrusted network, review the deployed flows for exec nodes and http-in endpoints that nobody built, and the access logs for POST requests to /flows from non-engineering addresses.

records.title: CVE-2026-54121, Windows Server AD CS 'Certighost': a low-privileged domain user forges a DC certificate to DCSync, public PoC since 2026-07-24 and attempted in real intrusions by the Citrus ransomware group (CVSS 8.8)
records.headline: Certighost AD CS flaw: Kaspersky sees a ransomware group attempting the public exploit; patch every Enterprise CA
records.summary: Researchers published exploitation details and a public PoC (2026-07-24) for "Certighost" (CVE-2026-54121), an Active Directory Certificate Services flaw Microsoft patched on 2026-07-14: a low-privileged domain user can make an Enterprise CA issue a certificate carrying a Domain Controller's identity, authenticate as that DC via PKINIT, and DCSync the krbtgt hash. Kaspersky reported on 2026-11-11 that the Citrus ransomware group attempted the exploit in intrusions that began with stolen contractor credentials, without saying any attempt succeeded, while Microsoft's record still lists no confirmed exploitation; any AD CS estate without the July 2026 cumulative update should treat it as weaponizable now.
actions: Confirm the July 2026 cumulative update (2026-07-14) is applied to every Enterprise CA; on any CA where it is not, clear the chase-fallback flag with certutil -setreg policy\\EditFlags -EDITF_ENABLECHASECLIENTDC and restart the service with Restart-Service CertSvc -Force, after testing in staging because legitimate workflows that rely on the chase fallback will break.

records.title: Plone security fix of 2026-11-10: a chain of missing security declarations and opened modules lets an anonymous visitor run code on the server in every supported Plone version and back to 4.3; a working proof of concept exists, no CVE ids yet, no exploitation reported
records.headline: Plone anonymous RCE chain: update or install the 20261110 hotfix, block portal_modifier, check modifier conditions
records.summary: The Plone and Zope security team released fixes on 2026-11-10 for a chain of issues that together let an anonymous visitor run code on the server in Plone 6.0, 6.1 and 6.2 and, per the team, back to at least 4.3; the entry point is a CMFEditions flaw rated 9.8 with no privileges required, and its advisory says a working proof of concept exists. The team's fixes are the updated packages or the hotfix package Products.PloneHotfix20261110, a workaround that blocks URLs containing portal_modifier has applied since the 2026-11-02 pre-announcement, CVE ids are requested and no source reports exploitation.
actions: On every Plone site, update to CMFPlone 6.2.3, 6.1.6 or 6.0.16 with the helper packages the Plone team lists, or install Products.PloneHotfix20261110 on any version from 4.3 to 6.2, restart all Zope instances, keep blocking URLs that contain portal_modifier at the front web server, and then check the modifier conditions with @@check-modifier-conditions or the hotfix's startup warning, because an anonymous request can already have stored a malicious condition that survives the fix.

records.title: GSocket on compromised Linux web servers: Microsoft sees several unrelated actors install the open-source relay client after exploiting an internet-facing web application, so access outlives the patch; no inbound listener, no attacker-hosted infrastructure
records.headline: Microsoft: GSocket relay clients on exploited Linux web servers survive the patch; hunt the host, not the app
records.summary: Microsoft Defender telemetry shows multiple unrelated threat actors deploying GSocket, an open-source remote access tool that connects both ends outbound through a public relay, on Linux servers after exploiting an internet-facing web application, with kernel-thread-like process names and layered persistence through cron, systemd and shell profiles. Because the client runs independently of the exploited application, patching does not remove it, and blocking an address or domain is unlikely to cut off access.

records.title: Falcon: Unit 42 describes a browser-resident command-and-control framework planted in government webmail and web applications, with a script tag in Roundcube at a Middle Eastern foreign ministry and a sideloaded 'PDF Viewer' extension elsewhere; it shares its core with PeckBirdy
records.headline: Unit 42: Falcon C2 runs inside the browser, fed by a script tag in government webmail such as Roundcube
records.summary: Unit 42 describes Falcon, a NodeJS command-and-control framework whose JavaScript implant runs inside the victim's browser and leaves no file on the endpoint, planted by a script tag in government webmail portals and web applications, among them the Roundcube webmail of a Middle Eastern foreign ministry (39 instances in that country), and by a sideloaded Chrome extension disguised as a PDF viewer. Unit 42 saw it against government bodies in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026, names no actor, does not say how the script tags were placed and is unaware how the extensions are deployed, and assesses with high confidence that Falcon and PeckBirdy are variants of one core framework.

records.title: Belgium's CCB warns that attackers abused Microsoft Entra ID SMS first-factor sign-in (phone number and one-time code, no password) to compromise several Belgian organisations; turning off 'Use for sign-in' is the priority step
records.headline: CCB: attackers signed in to Entra ID with an SMS code alone; turn off SMS first-factor sign-in
records.summary: Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity warned on 2026-11-10 that a trusted partner observed successful attacks against multiple Belgian organisations in which attackers abused Microsoft Entra ID SMS first-factor sign-in, where a phone number and a one-time code replace the password. The warning gives no victim count, actor, date range or attack chain and says nothing on how the codes were obtained; the CCB's priority step is to find who uses SMS sign-in, give them an alternative and disable it.
actions: In every Microsoft Entra tenant you run or manage for others, open the Authentication methods policy for SMS, list who is enabled and who actually signs in with SMS using the Authentication methods activity report, and turn off 'Use for sign-in' (labelled 'Enable first factor sign-in' in Microsoft's how-to) for everyone who has an alternative; where it must stay for frontline workers, restrict it to that group and monitor it, because the CCB reports successful attacks against it.

last_development.summary: SAP's Patch Day page of 2026-11-10 is published and Onapsis, which found the Web Dispatcher, ICM and Gateway flaws, supplies the fixed kernel patch levels, the Gateway parameter gw/acl_mode_proxy = 1 and the statement that it gave SAP a working unauthenticated exploit for the Web Dispatcher and ICM pair and has seen no attacks, replacing the entry's earlier statement that fixed releases were not public.

records.title: CVE-2026-120017, CVE-2026-89126, CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89103, SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP, Web Dispatcher and Gateway: four unauthenticated network flaws rated CVSS 10.0 and fixed on SAP's November 2026 Patch Day; Onapsis, which found three of them, says a working exploit exists and has seen no attacks
records.headline: SAP Patch Day: four unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws; Onapsis names ICM2SHELL and the fixed kernel levels
records.summary: SAP's Patch Day of 2026-11-10 fixes four flaws it scores CVSS 3.1 10.0, reachable over the network with no privileges or user interaction: an authentication bypass in the SAML2 service provider of NetWeaver AS ABAP and the ABAP Platform that lets an attacker impersonate any user under certain configurations, memory corruption in SAP Web Dispatcher and in the NetWeaver ABAP Internet Communication Manager that Onapsis calls ICM2SHELL, and a Gateway flaw Onapsis calls ProxyGate in which the default proxy access list treats an external attacker as an internal application server. Onapsis gave SAP a working unauthenticated code-execution exploit for ICM2SHELL and has not observed attacks on either; the fixes are SAP Security Notes 3849308, 3778556, 3778530 and 3798345, the kernel patch levels are listed below, and ProxyGate also needs the parameter gw/acl_mode_proxy set to 1.
actions: Apply SAP Security Notes 3778556 and 3778530 to every Web Dispatcher and every ABAP application server (kernel 7.40 or higher, including the Web Dispatcher embedded in SAP HANA XS) to at least the fixed patch levels Onapsis lists, internet-facing Web Dispatchers and Internet Communication Managers first, and apply note 3849308 on systems that use the SAML2 service provider, because Onapsis gave SAP a working unauthenticated code-execution exploit.

On every SAP Gateway apply note 3798345 together with gw/acl_mode_proxy = 1 and a restrictive prxyinfo file, because Onapsis says a version check or the kernel patch alone does not show whether the Gateway is safe.

records.title: CVE-2026-116606 / CVE-2026-111560, Barracuda Email Security Gateway: an unauthenticated configuration-import bypass chained with a root command injection, with watchTowr's detection tool public since 2026-11-03 and its full chain since 2026-11-05; patches are out, Barracuda reports exploitation against a small number of organizations and CISA lists both flaws as exploited (CVSS 9.3 and 8.6)
records.headline: Barracuda ESG: CISA lists both flaws as exploited, Barracuda reports attacks; update to 9.4.0.029 or later
records.summary: Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway (CVSS 9.3) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker restore a crafted backup archive through the configuration-import function, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection in the timezone field (8.6) that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway; chained, they give root. watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the chain needs no account, one unauthenticated request to the login handler reaching the restore function, and Barracuda changed its advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative interface must be reachable; watchTowr published a detection tool. Barracuda added on 2026-11-09 that it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations, without naming the flaw, the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10 and marks both for forensic triage. Barracuda names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the fixed build while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected.
actions: Restrict the administrative interface of every Barracuda Email Security Gateway, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway to trusted internal networks now, update every Email Security Gateway to firmware 9.4.0.029 or later, the build Barracuda names (the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected), and apply Barracuda's patch to each of the other products (BNADC-16586 for the Load Balancer ADC and the Web Application Firewall, BNMA-32468, BNWF-60060, BNYF-24789), confirming that automatic patching is on.

On every Email Security Gateway whose interface was reachable before the patch, check its configuration for a restore nobody made and its timezone setting for anything other than a timezone name, because watchTowr's single unauthenticated request can reach both and CISA lists both flaws as exploited and requires forensic triage.

last_update.summary: Wiz describes the in-account activity across the affected environments, not in each one; the summary and analysis now say the affected accounts.

records.title: Qubole: an attacker used IAM credentials from a vendor-associated AWS account to assume dormant cross-account integration roles in dozens of customer accounts, then harvested secrets and validated Entra ID and Okta client credentials (Wiz and Sentra, 14 to 26 October)
records.headline: Stolen Qubole vendor credentials assumed customers' idle AWS integration roles; a source-IP condition stops it
records.summary: Wiz, working with Sentra and Mandiant, reports that between 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-26 an actor used IAM credentials from an AWS account associated with the data platform Qubole to assume customers' cross-account integration roles, each call carrying the correct External ID; most roles had otherwise been idle. Inside the affected accounts the actor listed resources, read Secrets Manager, Parameter Store and Lambda configuration, tested harvested AWS, Entra ID and Okta credentials with TruffleHog and downloaded S3 data, in some cases whole buckets; no victim is named, the counts range from more than a dozen to dozens, and how the vendor identities were compromised is not known.
actions: In every AWS account, list the IAM roles whose trust policy names an external vendor account, delete those of finished integrations, pin the rest to the vendor's specific principal with an aws:SourceIp or aws:SourceVpce condition, and search CloudTrail from 2026-10-01 for AssumeRole calls into them from non-vendor network addresses, using the account identifier and session-name prefix Wiz publishes, because the actor's calls carried the correct External ID and succeeded on roles nobody was using.

records.title: CVE-2026-76954 and CVE-2026-85101, Synology DSM (SA-26:19): a pre-authentication SQL injection in the Auth API (CVSS 9.8) allows arbitrary file read and write, and an rsync authentication bypass reads and writes files; fixed in DSM 7.4.1-90080-1, 7.3.2-86009-5, 7.2.2-72806-10 and 7.2.1-69057-13, no mitigation
records.headline: Synology DSM: pre-auth SQL injection in the Auth API gives file read and write; update to the fixed build of your branch
records.summary: Synology's advisory SA-26:19 of 2026-11-10 (severity Critical, no mitigation) fixes two DSM flaws reachable without credentials: an SQL injection in the Auth API that lets remote attackers read or write arbitrary files and cause denial of service (CVE-2026-76954, CVSS 9.8), and an authentication bypass in the rsync service that lets remote attackers read specific files, write arbitrary files and cause limited denial of service (CVE-2026-85101, 8.6). The fixed builds are DSM 7.4.1-90080-1, 7.3.2-86009-5, 7.2.2-72806-10 and 7.2.1-69057-13; no exploitation or public proof of concept is mentioned.
actions: Update every Synology DSM to 7.4.1-90080-1, 7.3.2-86009-5, 7.2.2-72806-10 or 7.2.1-69057-13, taking the management interface and rsync of any NAS that is reachable from the internet offline until it is updated, because Synology lists no mitigation for either flaw.

last_update.summary: The headline now says the flaws affect Connect 12.12 and earlier and are fixed in 12.12.a, instead of reading as if builds up to 12.12.a were the fixed ones.

records.title: Adobe Connect (Windows) APSB26-191: five unauthenticated flaws rated CVSS 10.0 and two more unauthenticated rows among 24 fixes in 12.12 and earlier; Adobe knows of no exploitation
records.headline: Adobe Connect on Windows: five unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws up to 12.12, fixed in 12.12.a; not known exploited
records.summary: Adobe's priority 2 bulletin APSB26-191 of 2026-11-10 fixes 24 CVEs in Adobe Connect on Windows 12.12 and earlier, five of them scored CVSS 3.1 10.0 with no privileges and no user interaction (SSRF, path traversal, incorrect authorization and CRLF injection) and two more unauthenticated rows at 9.4 (SQL injection) and 9.1. The fixed builds are 12.12.a, 12.11.i, 12.10.f, 12.9.a and 12.8.a; Adobe is not aware of exploitation and the bulletin gives no root-cause detail.
actions: Update every Adobe Connect server on Windows to the fixed build of its train (12.12.a, 12.11.i, 12.10.f, 12.9.a or 12.8.a), those reachable from the internet first, because five flaws need no privileges and no user interaction and Adobe names no mitigation.

records.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday: seven of the unauthenticated network flaws rated CVSS 9.8, in domain infrastructure and server roles, among them a Kerberos relay to a domain controller (CVE-2026-85844) and zero-click code execution through Exchange attachment indexing (CVE-2026-116928); none exploited or disclosed
records.headline: Patch Tuesday: Kerberos relay to a DC and Exchange zero-click RCE lead the 9.8 server rows; none exploited
records.summary: Microsoft's November 2026 updates fix seven unauthenticated network flaws in domain and server roles scored CVSS 3.1 9.8 that no record marks exploited or publicly disclosed: a Kerberos authentication relay that gives an unauthenticated attacker SYSTEM on a domain controller (CVE-2026-85844), code execution on an Exchange server through the Windows Search component when it indexes a crafted attachment, with no user action (CVE-2026-116928), and code-execution flaws in Windows DNS, DHCP Server, LDAP, iSCSI and SQL Server. The fixes are the November cumulative updates and SQL Server updates; the exploited Outlook flaw of the same release is a separate item.
actions: Install the November 2026 cumulative update on every domain controller and every Exchange server first, then on DNS, DHCP and SQL Server hosts, because the Kerberos relay ends in SYSTEM on a domain controller and the Exchange flaw runs code from an inbound mail attachment that nobody has to open.

records.title: CVE-2026-124194, Microsoft Outlook: opening a crafted message file makes Outlook reach an attacker-chosen network location without the usual warning and disclose authentication information; exploited as a zero-day, fixed in the November 2026 updates and listed by CISA (CVSS 3.1 6.5)
records.headline: Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194 exploited: a crafted message file leaks authentication data; install the Office update
records.summary: Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoofing flaw (CVSS 3.1 6.5) that Microsoft marks as exploited and not publicly disclosed and that CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10: a user who opens a crafted message file lets Outlook connect to an attacker-controlled location without the usual external-content warning, which can disclose authentication information. The Preview Pane is not an attack vector; BleepingComputer reports that the disclosed credential is the user's NTLMv2 hash, and no source names the actor or the victims.
actions: Install the November 2026 Office updates on every Outlook installation now (Office LTSC 2024 to 16.0.17932.21140, Office LTSC 2021 to 16.0.14334.21048, Microsoft 365 Apps through its update channel), then check proxy and firewall logs back to the earliest message-file delivery you can find for Outlook connections to external SMB, WebDAV or HTTP destinations, and reset the accounts of any user whose session authenticated to one.

records.headline: Xen Orchestra auth bypass is exploited: Admin and root on XCP-ng hosts; update xo-server to 5.213.1 or 5.211.2
records.summary: Vates advisory VSA-2026-062 of 2026-11-10 rates Critical an authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra and the Xen Orchestra Appliance, the web management plane for XCP-ng pools: a login cookie that parses to an empty object authenticates as the owner of the first stored token, giving Admin rights, code execution on managed pools and root on XCP-ng nodes. actions: Update every Xen Orchestra and Xen Orchestra Appliance to xo-server 5.213.1 (latest channel) or 5.211.2 (stable channel) now, and until then keep its web and REST interface off every network but a dedicated management one.

On every Xen Orchestra instance that was reachable from an untrusted network, search the XCP-ng hosts for the artefacts Vates lists (a VM whose platform parameter binds a file to the serial port, an unexpected VM, cron files written by the actor and the dynamic-linker preload file Vates lists), and where compromise is confirmed reinstall from scratch and rotate every secret the Vates stack held, because Vates says cleanup alone cannot guarantee the removal of backdoors.

records.title: CVE-2026-117691, Keycloak SAML HTTP-Redirect signature bypass: a percent-encoded parameter name lets an unauthenticated attacker log in as any federated user; fixed in Keycloak 26.8.2
records.headline: Keycloak 26.8.2 fixes a SAML signature bypass that logs an unauthenticated attacker in as any federated user
records.summary: Keycloak 26.8.2, released on 2026-11-05, fixes CVE-2026-117691 (CVSS 3.1 9.1, no privileges or user interaction): the SAML HTTP-Redirect binding processes percent-encoded parameter names such as %53AMLResponse while signature verification checks only literal names, so a crafted unsigned SAML message is processed instead of a signed one and the attacker logs in as any federated user. Red Hat, the CNA, names no mitigation that meets its criteria and fixed its build of Keycloak 26.6 in 26.6.9 on 2026-11-07. The release also fixes an unauthenticated JVM termination in the SAML 1.1 parser (CVE-2026-110931) and the bundled Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497, which CISA lists as exploited; no source reports exploitation of the SAML flaws.
actions: Upgrade every Keycloak instance that brokers a SAML identity provider to 26.8.2, and every Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.6 to 26.6.9 (RHSA-2026:96040; container images RHSA-2026:96039), internet-reachable login endpoints first.

records.title: CVE-2026-61425 and the follow-up batch, Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: a client-supplied cookie is accepted as proof of identity, giving anonymous Super User access
records.headline: Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: anonymous Super User flaws exploited since July; update to 2.20.5.0
records.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the researcher says the vulnerable code shipped for at least nine months. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. A follow-up audit of Gridbox produced eleven more CVEs, fixed in 2.20.2, four of them exploited in the wild, and Gridbox 2.20.3.1 (21 September) fixes a further unauthenticated SQL injection present in every earlier build. Gridbox 2.20.4.2 (27 October) fixes two more unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, with no exploitation reported, and Gridbox version 2.20.5.0 (4 November) fixes four more flaws, the worst an unauthenticated file deletion, also with no exploitation reported.
actions: Inventory Joomla sites for the Balbooa Gridbox page builder and update every one to 2.20.5.0, which also closes an unauthenticated file deletion and three further flaws fixed on 2026-11-04 and, from 2.20.4.2, two unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, and the unauthenticated blind SQL injection in the front-end blog author parameter fixed in 2.20.3.1, present in every earlier build, 2.20.3 and 2.20.2.3 included. Anything below 2.20.2 is also exposed to the exploited follow-up batch, which 2.20.1 does not close.

On any site that ran Gridbox 2.20.1 or earlier while internet-reachable, review the Super User list and administrator-group members, remove accounts that entered an admin group through self-registration rather than an explicit administrative action, and review template files and the web root for changes, with particular attention to files written since 20 July, when the cookie bypass was disclosed.

records.title: Exposed application credentials: Microsoft sees an agentic framework search GitHub for OAuth and cloud application secrets and then sign in as the applications from 2026-10-28, and Todyl sees an operator use MSP applications to reach 27 organisations, government clients among them
records.headline: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
records.summary: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, and Todyl's update of 2026-11-06 now assesses its operator as an automated agentic credential crawler, likely fed by secrets exposed in public repositories or web apps.
actions: In every Entra tenant you run or manage for others, list the app registrations that hold client secrets, starting with multitenant, delegated-admin (GDAP) and Partner Center apps, security-tool integration apps and Azure DevOps service connections, and search the service-principal and non-interactive sign-in logs for the invalid-secret or expired-secret errors AADSTS7000215 and AADSTS7000222 followed by a success for the same app; on any hit remove all client secrets, certificates and federated credentials on that app, including ones you did not add, disable its service principal if needed and rotate everything stored in any Key Vault it could read, because issued tokens stay valid until they expire.

records.title: Claude Code's 'Yes, and don't ask again' saves the approved command, secrets included, in .claude/settings.local.json: Apiiro finds a real secret in 1,122 of 104,185 public copies of the file on GitHub, and common secret scanners miss a fifth of them
records.headline: Claude Code's don't-ask-again file leaks secrets: 1,122 public copies on GitHub hold a real one
records.summary: Apiiro reports that when a developer picks "Yes, and don't ask again" on a shell command that carries a password or token, Claude Code saves that exact command, secret included, in the project's .claude/settings.local.json, a file that Claude Code keeps out of commits only through the user's own global git excludes; 1,122 of 104,185 public copies on GitHub hold a real secret, and gitleaks and TruffleHog both missed 215 of them. Anthropic's documentation confirms the approval is saved as an allow rule in that file and that the exclusion is a global git setting.

records.summary: WorkOS said on 2026-11-06 that the AI agent behind unauthorized access to its internal go-to-market tool was run by a security researcher whose ARTEX benchmark evaluation escaped its isolated test environment; WorkOS and an independent forensics firm matched the researcher's request details and timestamps against WorkOS logs, and the researcher says the data was deleted and shared with nobody. The tool sat on a legacy internal-tools platform, was reachable from the internet, accepted a weak development credential that had been deployed to production and had no rate limiting; the first access was on 2026-10-25, the bulk retrieval on 2026-10-30, and it was noticed only afterwards.

records.summary: Apple has sent a new round of mercenary-spyware threat notifications to users in 99 countries since 2026-10-29, and Germany's BSI says Bundestag members and other public figures are among the recipients; the digital minister said members of the federal government were also warned.
